sentences.zh: 浡泥，宋太宗時始通中國。

translations.literal: Brunei first established contact with China in the reign of Emperor Taizong of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Brunei first sent tribute to China during the reign of Song Taizong.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年八月命御史張敬之、福建行省都事沈秩往使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Hongwu, the Emperor ordered the censor Zhang Jingzhi and Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner Shen Zhi to go on a mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Hongwu year 3, the court appointed Censor Zhang Jingzhi and Fujian provincial commissioner Shen Zhi as envoys.

sentences.zh: 自泉州航海，閱半年抵阇婆，又逾月至其國。

translations.literal: They sailed from Quanzhou; after half a year they reached Java, and after another month more they arrived in the country.
translations.idiomatic: They put to sea from Quanzhou, reached Java after six months, and reached Brunei another month later.

sentences.zh: 王馬合謨沙傲慢不為禮，秩責之，始下座拜受詔。

translations.literal: The king Mahmud Shah was arrogant and showed no courtesy; Shen Zhi rebuked him, whereupon he left his seat and bowed to receive the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: King Mahmud Shah received them arrogantly until Shen Zhi reproved him; only then did the king rise from his seat and bow to accept the edict.

sentences.zh: 時其國為蘇祿所侵，頗衰耗，王辭以貧，請三年後入貢。

translations.literal: At that time the country was being invaded by Sulu and had declined considerably; the king pleaded poverty and asked to present tribute three years later.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was then under attack from Sulu and much weakened; the king cited poverty and asked to defer tribute for three years.

sentences.zh: 秩曉以大義，王既許諾，其國素屬阇婆，阇婆人間之，王意中沮。

translations.literal: Shen Zhi enlightened him with the larger principles of duty, and once the king had promised, since the country had long been subject to Java, the Javanese intervened and the king's resolve wavered.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhi admonished him on the obligations of allegiance, and after the king agreed, Javanese—among whom Brunei had long been counted—interfered and his purpose faltered.

sentences.zh: 秩折之曰：「阇婆久稱臣奉貢，爾畏阇婆，反不畏天朝邪？」

translations.literal: Shen Zhi pressed him, saying: "Java has long styled itself a subject and sent tribute—yet you fear Java and do not fear the Celestial Court?"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhi countered: "Java has long called itself a vassal and sent tribute. You fear Java, yet you do not fear the Celestial Court?

sentences.zh: 乃遣使奉表箋，貢鶴頂、生玳瑁、孔雀、梅花大片龍腦、米龍腦、西洋布、降真諸香。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent envoys with a memorial and letter of credence, presenting hornbill casques, raw tortoiseshell, peacocks, large-flake dragon's-blood incense, rice-grain dragon's-blood incense, Western cloth, and various eaglewood incenses.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched envoys bearing a memorial and credence, with tribute of hornbill casques, raw tortoiseshell, peacocks, large-flake and fine-grain dragon's-blood incense, Western cloth, and assorted eaglewoods.

sentences.zh: 八月從敬之等入朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month they entered court with Jingzhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month they entered court together with Zhang Jingzhi's party.

sentences.zh: 表用金，箋用銀，字近回鶻，皆鏤之以進。

translations.literal: The memorial was of gold and the letter of silver; the script resembled Uighur, and both were engraved for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was on gold and the letter on silver; the characters resembled Uighur script, and both were incised for presentation.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，宴賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and feasted and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and entertained them with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 八年命其國山川附祀福建山川之次。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he ordered the mountains and rivers of that country to be included in the secondary sacrifices to Fujian's mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the court ordered Brunei's mountains and rivers registered for secondary sacrifice alongside those of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年冬，其王麻那惹加那遣使入貢，乃遣官封為國王，賜印誥、敕符、勘合、錦綺、彩幣。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Yongle its king Maharaja Karna sent envoys with tribute, whereupon officials were dispatched to enfeoff him as king, granting a seal, patent of appointment, tally-slips, brocades, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Yongle year 3 King Maharaja Karna sent tribute; the court then enfeoffed him as king and bestowed a seal, patent, tally-slips, brocades, and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 王大悅，率妃及弟妹子女陪臣泛海來朝。

translations.literal: The king was greatly pleased and, with his consort and younger brothers, sisters, children, and attending ministers, crossed the sea to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed, the king sailed with his consort, siblings, children, and retinue to present himself at court.

sentences.zh: 次福建，守臣以聞。

translations.literal: They stopped at Fujian, and the local officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: They called at Fujian, and the guarding officials reported their arrival.

sentences.zh: 遣中官往宴賚，所過州縣皆宴。

translations.literal: The court sent eunuchs to feast and reward them, and every prefecture and county along the route held banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent eunuchs ahead to entertain them, and every prefecture and county on the route hosted feasts.

sentences.zh: 六年八月入都朝見，帝獎勞之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year they entered the capital and were received in audience; the Emperor commended and comforted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year 6 they reached the capital, were received in audience, and the emperor praised and comforted them.

sentences.zh: 王跪致詞曰：「陛下膺天寶命，統一萬方。

translations.literal: The king knelt and addressed the throne, saying: "Your Majesty has received Heaven's mandate and unifies the myriad regions.
translations.idiomatic: Kneeling, the king said: "Your Majesty, bearing Heaven's mandate, has united all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣遠在海島，荷蒙天恩，賜以封爵。

translations.literal: I dwell on a distant island and have received Heaven's grace in being granted a title of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: I live on a distant isle yet have been granted a noble title by imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 自是國中雨暘時順，歲屢豐登，民無災厲，山川之間，珍奇畢露，草木鳥獸，亦悉蕃育。

translations.literal: Since then rain and sunshine have been timely in our land, harvests have been abundant year after year, the people have been free of pestilence, rare things have appeared throughout the mountains, and plants and birds and beasts have all flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Since then our seasons have been fair, harvests plentiful, the people free of plague, wonders appearing in the hills, and every plant and creature thriving.

sentences.zh: 國中耆老咸謂此聖天子覆冒所致。

translations.literal: The elders of the country all say this is due to the encompassing shade of the sage Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Our elders all say this comes from the sage emperor's sheltering grace.

sentences.zh: 臣願睹天日之表，少輸悃誠，不憚險遠，躬率家屬陪臣，詣闕獻謝。」

translations.literal: I wished to behold the radiance of the sun and moon and offer a little of my sincere devotion, and, undaunted by distance and danger, have personally led my family and ministers to the palace to offer thanks."
translations.idiomatic: I longed to see your radiance and offer my devotion, and so, heedless of the perils of the voyage, I have brought my household and ministers to your gate in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 帝慰勞再三，命王妃所進中宮箋及方物，陳之文華殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly comforted him and ordered the consort's presentation to the inner palace and the local products displayed in the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him again and again, and had the consort's gifts to the inner palace and the tribute goods displayed in the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 王詣殿進獻畢，自王及妃以下悉賜冠帶、襲衣。

translations.literal: When the king had finished presenting his gifts in the hall, from the king and consort downward all were granted caps, belts, and robes of investiture.
translations.idiomatic: After the king had presented his gifts in the hall, he, the consort, and all below them received caps, belts, and investiture robes.

sentences.zh: 帝乃饗王於奉天門，妃以下饗於他所，禮訖送歸會同館。

translations.literal: The Emperor then feasted the king at Fengtian Gate; the consort and others were feasted elsewhere, and when the rites were concluded they were sent back to the Hostel for Tributary Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted the king at Fengtian Gate and the consort's party elsewhere; when the rites ended they returned to the Hostel for Tributary Envoys.

sentences.zh: 禮官請王見親王儀，帝令准公侯禮。

translations.literal: The ritual officials requested the protocol for the king's audience with princes; the Emperor ordered that the protocol for dukes and marquises be applied.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites asked what ceremony the king should use before the princes; the emperor ordered the etiquette accorded dukes and marquises.

sentences.zh: 尋賜王儀仗、交倚、銀器、傘扇、銷金鞍馬、金織文綺、紗羅、綾絹衣十襲，余賜賚有差。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he granted the king ceremonial guards, a folding chair, silver vessels, parasols and fans, gilded saddle and horse, gold-woven brocades, gauze, silk, and ten suits of clothing; the rest received gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: He soon granted the king ceremonial guards, a folding chair, silverware, parasols and fans, a gilded saddle and mount, gold-woven silks, gauzes, and ten suits of robes; others received gifts in due proportion.

sentences.zh: 十月，王卒於館。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the king died in the hostel.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the king died in the envoy hostel.

sentences.zh: 帝哀悼，輟朝三日，遣官致祭，賻以繒帛。

translations.literal: The Emperor mourned him, suspended court for three days, sent officials to offer sacrifice, and gave funeral gifts of silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, halted court for three days, sent officers to sacrifice, and bestowed silken funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 東宮親王皆遣祭，有司具棺郭、明器，葬之安德門外石子岡

translations.literal: The heir apparent and the princes all sent sacrifices; the relevant offices provided coffin, outer coffin, and spirit objects, and buried him outside Ande Gate at Shizigang
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and princes all sent offerings; the offices furnished coffin, outer case, and grave goods and buried him outside Ande Gate at Shizigang

sentences.zh: 〈現有渤泥國王墓，位於南京市雨花臺區〉

translations.literal: 〈The existing tomb of the king of Brunei stands in Yuhuatai District, Nanjing.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The tomb of the king of Brunei still stands in Yuhuatai District, Nanjing.〉

sentences.zh: ，樹碑神道。

translations.literal: , and erected a stele on the spirit way.
translations.idiomatic: and set up a spirit-way stele.

sentences.zh: 又建祠墓側，有司春秋祀以少牢，謚曰恭順。

translations.literal: A shrine was also built beside the tomb; the offices sacrificed there each spring and autumn with the lesser victim, and he was given the posthumous title Gongshun.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built beside the tomb as well; each spring and autumn the offices offered the lesser victim, and he was posthumously titled Gongshun.

sentences.zh: 賜敕慰其子遐旺，命襲封國王。

translations.literal: An edict of consolation was granted to his son Xiawang, ordering him to succeed to the enfeoffment as king.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of comfort was sent to his son Xiawang, commanding him to inherit the kingship.

sentences.zh: 遐旺與其叔父上言：「臣歲供爪哇片腦四十斤，乞敕爪哇罷歲供，歲進天朝。

translations.literal: Xiawang and his uncle submitted a petition: "Our country yearly supplies Java with forty catties of camphor flakes; we beg an edict to Java to cease this yearly levy and let us present it yearly to the Celestial Court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiawang and his uncle petitioned: "We yearly supply Java forty catties of camphor; we beg an edict that Java cease taking it so we may present it yearly to the court.

sentences.zh: 臣今歸國，乞命護送，就留鎮一年，慰國人之望。

translations.literal: When I return home, I beg that I be escorted and allowed to remain and administer the realm for one year to satisfy my people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: On my return I beg an escort and leave to remain one year and reassure my people.

sentences.zh: 並乞定朝貢期及傔從人數。」

translations.literal: We also beg that the schedule of tribute missions and the number of attendants be fixed."
translations.idiomatic: We also ask that the tribute schedule and the size of our retinue be set.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之，命三年一貢，傔從惟王所遣，遂敕爪哇國免其歲供。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented to all of it, ordering tribute once every three years and attendants only as many as the king might send, and also commanded Java to remit the yearly levy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted everything: tribute every three years, attendants at the king's discretion, and an edict exempting them from Java's yearly demand.

sentences.zh: 王辭歸，賜玉帶一、金百兩、銀三千兩及錢鈔、錦綺、紗羅、衾褥、帳幔、器物，余皆有賜。

translations.literal: When the king took leave to return, he was granted one jade belt, one hundred taels of gold, three thousand taels of silver, paper money, brocades, gauze, silk, quilts, curtains, and utensils; the others also received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the king received a jade belt, a hundred taels of gold, three thousand of silver, paper money, brocades, gauzes, silks, bedding, hangings, and utensils; the rest were rewarded in proportion.

sentences.zh: 以中官張謙、行人周航護行。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhang Qian and the courier Zhou Hang were sent to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhang Qian and courier Zhou Hang were appointed escorts.

sentences.zh: 初，故王言：「臣蒙恩賜爵，臣境土悉屬職方，乞封國之後山為一方鎮。」

translations.literal: Earlier the late king had said: "I have received grace in being enfeoffed, and all my territory now belongs to the Registers of the Realm; I beg that the rear mountain of the country be enfeoffed as a guardian peak of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The late king had said: "Having received a title, my whole domain lies within the imperial registers; I beg that our kingdom's rear mountain be enfeoffed as a guardian peak.

sentences.zh: 新王復以為言，乃封為長寧鎮國之山。

translations.literal: The new king repeated the request, and it was enfeoffed as the Ever-tranquil Mountain That Guards the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: The new king asked again, and the mountain was enfeoffed as the Ever-tranquil Mountain That Guards the Realm.

sentences.zh: 御製碑文，令謙等勒碑其上。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself composed the inscription and ordered Qian and the others to carve it on the stone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed the text himself and ordered Qian and his party to cut it into the stone.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The inscription reads:

sentences.zh: “上天祐啟我國家萬世無疆之基，誕命我太祖高皇帝全撫天下，休養生息，以治以教，仁聲義問，薄極照臨，四方萬國，奔走臣服，充湊於廷。

translations.literal: " Heaven blessed and inaugurated the foundation of our state for ten thousand generations without end, and charged my Grand Ancestor the August Emperor to embrace and pacify all under heaven, nourishing life and letting the people rest, governing and teaching them, so that humane renown and righteous inquiry spread to the utmost limit and shone upon all, and the myriad states of the four quarters hurried to submit and thronged the court."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven blessed our dynasty with an everlasting foundation and charged my Grand Ancestor to pacify all under heaven, to nourish life and teach the people, until humane fame and righteous renown reached every quarter and the myriad states hurried to court."

sentences.zh: 神化感動之機，其妙如此。

translations.literal: " The workings of divine transformation and responsive feeling are wondrous in this way."
translations.idiomatic: "Such is the wonder of transforming influence and responsive feeling."

sentences.zh: 朕嗣守鴻圖，率由典式。

translations.literal: " I have succeeded to the great design and follow the established pattern."
translations.idiomatic: "I have inherited the great enterprise and follow the established pattern."

sentences.zh: 嚴恭祗畏，協和所統。

translations.literal: " With solemn reverence I harmonize all I rule."
translations.idiomatic: "In solemn reverence I harmonize all I rule."

sentences.zh: 無間內外，均視一體。

translations.literal: " Without distinction of inner and outer, I regard all as one body."
translations.idiomatic: "Without distinction of near and far, I regard all as one body."

sentences.zh: 遐邇綏寧，亦克承予意。

translations.literal: " The distant and near are tranquil, and this too fulfills my intent."
translations.idiomatic: "Far and near are at peace, and this too fulfills my intent."

sentences.zh: 乃者浡泥國王，誠敬之至，知所尊崇，慕尚聲教，益謹益虔，率其眷屬、陪臣，不遠數萬里，浮海來朝，達其志，通其欲，稽顙陳辭曰：「遠方臣妾，丕冒天子之恩，以養以息，既庶且安。

translations.literal: " Now the king of Brunei, in utmost sincerity and respect, knows what to honor, admires and esteems our civilizing influence, and grows ever more careful and devout, leading his kin and attending ministers across many tens of thousands of li by sea to court, to express his will and communicate his desires, bowing his forehead to the ground and declaring: "We distant subjects, greatly covered by the Son of Heaven's grace, are nourished and given rest, and are already numerous and at peace.
translations.idiomatic: "The king of Brunei, in utmost sincerity, honors our teaching, grows ever more reverent, and with kin and ministers crossed the sea from afar, bowing low to say: "We distant subjects, sheltered by the Son of Heaven, are nourished and at peace.

sentences.zh: 思見日月之光，故不憚險遠，輒敢造廷。」

translations.literal: We long to behold the radiance of sun and moon; therefore we do not shrink from peril and distance, but dare to come to the court."
translations.idiomatic: We yearn to see the light of sun and moon; heedless of danger we have come to court."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「覆我者天，載我者地。

translations.literal: He also said: "Heaven covers me; earth bears me.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Heaven covers me; earth bears me.

sentences.zh: 使我有土地人民之奉，田疇邑井之聚，宮室之居，妻妾之樂，和味宜服，利用備器，以資其生，強罔敢侵，眾罔敢暴，實惟天子之賜。

translations.literal: He has given me the sustenance of land and people, the gathering of fields and hamlets, dwellings in palaces, the joy of wives and concubines, flavors suited to dress, useful implements prepared—everything to sustain life; the strong dare not invade us, the multitude dare not oppress us—this is truly the Son of Heaven's gift.
translations.idiomatic: He has given us land and people, fields and towns, palaces and households, wives and concubines, fitting food and dress, and every useful thing; the strong dare not invade us and the many dare not harm us—all this is the Son of Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 是天子功德所加，與天地並。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's meritorious grace is added to us and stands with heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's grace stands with heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 然天仰剛見，地蹐則履，惟天子遠而難見，誠有所不通。

translations.literal: Yet heaven, when one looks up, is seen; earth, when one treads upon it, is felt underfoot—only the Son of Heaven is far and hard to behold, and sincerity cannot fully reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is seen when we look up; earth is felt when we tread—but the Son of Heaven is far and hard to see, and our sincerity cannot fully reach him.

sentences.zh: 是以遠方臣妾，不敢自外，逾歷山海，躬詣闕延，以伸其悃。」

translations.literal: Therefore we distant subjects dare not hold ourselves apart; crossing mountains and seas, we come in person to the palace gate to express our sincere hearts."
translations.idiomatic: So we distant subjects dare not stand apart; crossing seas and mountains we come to the gate to lay bare our hearts."

sentences.zh: 朕曰：「惟天，惟皇考，付予以天下，子養庶民。

translations.literal: I said: "Heaven and my August Father have entrusted the empire to me to nurture the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I replied: "Heaven and my August Father have given me the empire to nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 天與皇考，視民同仁，予其承天與皇考之德，惟恐弗堪，弗若汝言。」

translations.literal: Heaven and my August Father regard the people with equal benevolence; I must carry forward the virtue of Heaven and my August Father—I fear I cannot bear it; I am not as you say."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and my August Father love the people alike; I must carry on their virtue—I fear I am unequal to it; your words are too generous."

sentences.zh: 乃又拜手稽首曰：「自天子建元之載，臣國時和歲豐，山川之藏，珍寶流溢，草木之無葩者皆華而實，異禽和鳴，走獸蹌舞。

translations.literal: He again bowed with hands joined and forehead to the ground, saying: "Since Your Majesty established the reign era, our country has enjoyed timely rain and abundant years; treasures have overflowed from the mountains; plants that had no blossoms have flowered and borne fruit; strange birds sing in harmony; running beasts dance with measured steps.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed again and said: "Since Your Majesty's reign our land has known fair seasons and rich harvests; treasures pour from the hills; barren plants flower and fruit; strange birds sing and beasts dance.

sentences.zh: 國之黃叟咸曰，中國聖人德化漸暨，斯多嘉應。

translations.literal: The yellow-haired elders of the country all say that the sage of China's transforming virtue has gradually reached us, and these many blessed responses have appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Our grey-haired elders say the sage of China's transforming virtue has reached us and these blessings have followed.

sentences.zh: 臣土雖遠，實天子之氓，故奮然而來覲也。」

translations.literal: Though my land is far, we are truly the Son of Heaven's subjects; therefore I have come eagerly to pay court."
translations.idiomatic: Though our land is far, we are the Son of Heaven's people; that is why I have come eagerly to court."

sentences.zh: 朕觀其言文貌恭，動不逾則，悅喜禮教，脫略夷習，非超然卓異者不能。

translations.literal: I observed that his words were courteous in text and bearing, his movements never exceeding the rule; he delighted in ritual and teaching and cast off barbarian habits—none but one surpassingly exceptional could do this."
translations.idiomatic: I saw that his words and bearing were reverent, his conduct measured; he delighted in ritual and shed barbarian ways—only an extraordinary man could do this."

sentences.zh: 稽之載籍，自古逷遠之國，奉若天道，仰服聲教，身致帝廷者有之。

translations.literal: " Consulting the records, from antiquity there have been states far away that honored Heaven's way, looked up to our civilizing influence, and came in person to the imperial court."
translations.idiomatic: "In the records, distant states have honored Heaven's way, revered our teaching, and come in person to court."

sentences.zh: 至於舉妻子、兄弟、親戚、陪臣頓首稱臣妾於階陛之下者，惟浡泥國王一人；

translations.literal: " But as for bringing wife and children, brothers, kin, and attending ministers to bow their heads and call themselves subjects and handmaids below the steps—only the king of Brunei has done this;"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet to bring wife and children, brothers, kin, and ministers to bow as subjects below the steps—only the king of Brunei has done this;"

sentences.zh: 西南諸蕃國長，未有如王賢者。

translations.literal: " among the chieftains of the southwestern barbarian states, none has been as worthy as this king."
translations.idiomatic: Among the chieftains of the southwestern realms, none has equaled this king.

sentences.zh: 王之至誠貫於金石，達於神明，而令名傳於悠久，可謂有光顯矣。

translations.literal: " The king's utmost sincerity penetrates metal and stone and reaches the spirits; his fair name will be transmitted for long ages—this may be called glorious indeed."
translations.idiomatic: "His sincerity pierces metal and stone and moves the spirits; his fame will endure—this is truly glorious."

sentences.zh: 茲特錫封王國中之山為張寧鎮國之山，賜文刻石，以著王休，於昭萬年，其永無斁。

translations.literal: " Now we specially grant and enfeoff the mountain in the midst of his kingdom as the Ever-tranquil Mountain That Guards the Realm, bestowing a text carved in stone to manifest the king's repose, shining for ten thousand years, never to cease."
translations.idiomatic: "We now enfeoff the mountain at the heart of his kingdom as the Ever-tranquil Mountain That Guards the Realm, with an inscribed stone to show the king's repose, bright for ten thousand years without end."

sentences.zh: 系之詩曰：「炎海之墟，浡泥所處。

translations.literal: " A poem is appended, which reads: "In the wastes of the fiery sea, where Brunei lies.
translations.idiomatic: "A poem is appended: "In the wastes of the fiery sea lies Brunei.

sentences.zh: 煦仁漸義，有順無迕。

translations.literal: Warming benevolence and gradual righteousness—there is compliance, no defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Warmed by benevolence, steeped in righteousness—compliant, never rebellious.

sentences.zh: 撦撦賢王，惟化之慕。

translations.literal: Earnest and worthy king, who admires only transformation.
translations.idiomatic: An earnest and worthy king, who cherishes only civilization.

sentences.zh: 導以象胥，遹來奔赴。

translations.literal: Guided by interpreters, he hastens to come.
translations.idiomatic: Led by interpreters, he hastens to court.

sentences.zh: 同其婦子、兄弟、陪臣，稽顙闕下，有言以陳。

translations.literal: With wife and children, brothers, and attending ministers, he bows his forehead below the gate and has words to declare.
translations.idiomatic: With wife and children, brothers, and ministers he bows below the gate and speaks his mind.

sentences.zh: 謂君猶天，遺以休樂，一視同仁，匪偏厚薄。

translations.literal: He says the lord is like heaven, bestowing repose and joy, treating all alike, not partial or uneven.
translations.idiomatic: He says the lord is like heaven, granting peace and joy, viewing all alike without favor.

sentences.zh: 顧茲鮮德，弗稱所云。

translations.literal: But I, considering my slight virtue, do not match what he says.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I, of slight virtue, do not deserve such words.

sentences.zh: 浪舶風檣，實勞懇勤。

translations.literal: Wave-borne ships and wind-filled sails—how earnest and toilsome his labor.
translations.idiomatic: Ships on the waves and sails in the wind—how earnest his toil.

sentences.zh: 稽古遠臣，順來怒ＤＭ。

translations.literal: Examining antiquity, distant ministers who came in submission would depart when angered.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, envoys from afar who came in homage would turn back at the slightest offense.

sentences.zh: 以躬或難，矧曰家室。

translations.literal: For oneself the journey might be hard—how much more with one's household.
translations.idiomatic: For oneself the road was hardship enough—how much more with wife and children.

sentences.zh: 王心亶誠，金石其堅。

translations.literal: The king's heart is utterly sincere, firm as metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: This king's heart is utterly sincere, firm as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 西南蕃長，疇與王賢。

translations.literal: Among the chieftains of the southwestern barbarians, who compares with this king?
translations.idiomatic: Among southwestern chieftains, who compares with this king?

sentences.zh: 矗矗高山，以鎮王國。

translations.literal: Towering, towering—the high mountain that guards the kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Towering stands the mountain that guards the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 镵文於石，懋昭王德。

translations.literal: Text is cut into stone to make the king's virtue illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: Words are carved in stone to glorify the king's virtue.

sentences.zh: 王德克昭，王國攸寧。

translations.literal: The king's virtue can shine forth; the kingdom will thereby be at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the king's virtue shines, the kingdom is at peace.

sentences.zh: 於萬斯年，仰我大明。」

translations.literal: For ten thousand years, look up to our Great Ming."
translations.idiomatic: For ten thousand years, look up to our Great Ming."

sentences.zh: 八年九月遣使從謙等入貢謝恩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year envoys were sent with Qian and the others to enter court and offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 8 envoys came with Zhang Qian's party to court to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 明年覆命謙賜其王錦綺、紗羅、彩絹凡百二十匹，其下皆有賜。

translations.literal: The next year Qian was again sent with orders to grant the king one hundred twenty bolts of brocade, gauze, silk, and colored silk in all; those below him also received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Qian was again sent to grant the king one hundred twenty bolts of brocade, gauze, silk, and colored silk; his subordinates were rewarded in proportion.

sentences.zh: 十年九月，遐旺偕其母來朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the tenth year Xiawang came to court with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 10 Xiawang came to court with his mother.

sentences.zh: 命禮官宴之會同館，光祿寺旦暮給酒饌。

translations.literal: The Board of Rites was ordered to feast them at the Hostel for Tributary Envoys, and the Court of Imperial Entertainments supplied food morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites feasted them at the tributary hostel while the Court of Imperial Entertainments supplied meals morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝饗之奉天門，王母亦有宴。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor feasted them at Fengtian Gate, and the queen mother also received a feast.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor feasted them at Fengtian Gate, and the queen mother was feasted separately.

sentences.zh: 越二日，再宴，賜王冠帶、襲衣，王母、王叔父以下，分賜有差。

translations.literal: Two days later they were feasted again; the king was granted cap, belt, and investiture robe, and the queen mother, the king's uncle, and those below received gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they were feasted again; the king received cap, belt, and robe, and the queen mother, uncle, and others gifts in due measure.

sentences.zh: 明年二月辭歸。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year they took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the next year they departed.

sentences.zh: 賜金百，銀五百，鈔三千錠，錢千五百緡，錦四，綺帛紗羅八十，金織文繡、文綺衣各一，衾褥、幃幔、器物咸具。

translations.literal: They were granted one hundred taels of gold, five hundred of silver, three thousand ingots of paper money, fifteen hundred strings of cash, four pieces of brocade, eighty of silk, gauze, and damask, one suit each of gold-woven brocade and patterned silk, and quilts, curtains, and utensils in full.
translations.idiomatic: They received a hundred taels of gold, five hundred of silver, three thousand ingots of paper money, fifteen hundred strings of cash, four brocades, eighty pieces of silk and gauze, gold-woven robes, bedding, hangings, and full sets of utensils.

sentences.zh: 自十三年至洪熙元年四入貢，後貢使漸稀。

translations.literal: From the thirteenth year to the first year of Hongxi they presented tribute four times; afterward tribute missions grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: From year 13 through Hongxi year 1 they sent tribute four times; thereafter missions grew infrequent.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，給事中王希文言：「暹羅、佔城、琉球、爪哇、浡泥五國來貢，並道東莞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing the supervising secretary Wang Xiwen said: "Siam, Champa, Ryukyu, Java, and Brunei came to offer tribute, all traveling by way of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 9 Supervising Secretary Wang Xiwen memorialized: "Siam, Champa, Ryukyu, Java, and Brunei all came by way of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 後因私攜賈客，多絕其貢。

translations.literal: Later, because they privately brought merchants along, tribute was largely cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Later they privately carried merchants and tribute largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 正德間，佛郎機闌入流毒，概行屏絕。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period the Folangji forcibly entered and spread harm, and they were generally shut out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde the Portuguese forced entry and did harm, and access was broadly barred.

sentences.zh: 曾未幾年，遽爾議復，損威已甚。」

translations.literal: Within only a few years there was talk of reopening it—authority had already been much diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years there was talk of reopening trade—prestige had already suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 章下都察院，請悉遵舊制，毋許混冒。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Censorate, which requested strict adherence to the old regulations and no admixture or false claims."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Censorate, which urged strict observance of the old rules and no false or mixed traffic.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，其王卒，無嗣，族人爭立。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period the king died without an heir, and clansmen fought over the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign the king died without an heir and clansmen fought for the throne.

sentences.zh: 國中殺戮幾盡，乃立其女為王。

translations.literal: Nearly the whole country was slaughtered before they enthroned his daughter as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Slaughter nearly consumed the realm before they enthroned his daughter as ruler.

sentences.zh: 漳州人張姓者，初為其國那督，華言尊官也，因亂出奔。

translations.literal: A man surnamed Zhang from Zhangzhou had originally been nadatu in that country—a high office in Chinese parlance—and fled abroad because of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhangzhou man, once the kingdom's nadatu—a title meaning a high minister in Chinese usage—had fled during the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 女主立，迎還之。

translations.literal: When the female ruler was enthroned, she welcomed him back.
translations.idiomatic: When the queen regnant took power, she recalled him.

sentences.zh: 其女出入王宮，得心疾，妄言父有反謀。

translations.literal: His daughter went in and out of the royal palace; she developed a mental disorder and falsely said her father harbored treasonous designs.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter, who frequented the palace, fell ill in mind and falsely accused her father of plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 女主懼，遣人按問其家，那督自殺。

translations.literal: The female ruler was afraid and sent men to investigate his household; the nadatu killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The queen, alarmed, sent investigators to his house; the nadatu took his own life.

sentences.zh: 國人為訟冤，女主悔，絞殺其女，授其子官。

translations.literal: The people pleaded his innocence; the female ruler repented, strangled her daughter, and gave his son an office.
translations.idiomatic: The people petitioned for justice; the queen repented, executed her daughter by strangulation, and appointed the man's son to office.

sentences.zh: 後雖不復朝貢，而商人往來不絕。

translations.literal: Although tribute missions did not resume, merchants traveled back and forth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Though tribute ceased, merchant traffic never stopped.

sentences.zh: 國統十四洲，在舊港之西，自佔城四十日可至。

translations.literal: The realm comprises fourteen districts; it lies west of Old Port and can be reached from Champa in forty days.
translations.idiomatic: The country has fourteen districts, west of Old Port, forty days' sail from Champa.

sentences.zh: 初屬爪哇，後屬暹羅，改名大泥。

translations.literal: At first it was subject to Java, later to Siam, and its name was changed to Dani.
translations.idiomatic: It had first been under Java, then under Siam, and was renamed Dani.

sentences.zh: 華人多流寓其地。

translations.literal: Many Chinese sojourned there.
translations.idiomatic: Many Chinese lived there as settlers.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，閩、粵海寇遺孽逋逃至此，積二千餘人。

translations.literal: At the end of Jiajing, remnants of Fujian and Guangdong sea bandits fled there and numbered more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jiajing, Fujian and Guangdong pirates' remnants fled there and grew to more than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，紅毛番強商其境，築土庫以居。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period the Dutch forcibly traded in its territory and built earthen forts to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the Dutch forced trade and built fortified warehouses on its soil.

sentences.zh: 其入彭湖互市者，所攜乃大泥國文也。

translations.literal: Those who went to Penghu to trade carried documents of the Dani state.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants trading at Penghu bore papers issued by Dani.

sentences.zh: 諸風俗、物產，具詳《宋史》。

translations.literal: Customs and products are fully detailed in the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Its customs and products are set out fully in the History of Song.

sentences.zh: 滿剌加

translations.literal: Malacca
translations.idiomatic: Malacca

sentences.zh: 滿剌加，在佔城南。

translations.literal: Malacca lies south of Champa.
translations.idiomatic: Malacca lies south of Champa.

sentences.zh: 順風八日至龍牙門，又西行二日即至。

translations.literal: With a fair wind one reaches Longyamen in eight days, and in two more days sailing west one arrives.
translations.idiomatic: With fair winds it is eight days to Longyamen and two more westward to the port.

sentences.zh: 或云即古頓遜，唐哥羅富沙。

translations.literal: Some say it is ancient Tun-sun and Tang's Keluofusha.
translations.idiomatic: Some identify it with ancient Tun-sun and Tang's Keluofusha.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年十月遣中官尹慶使其地，賜以織金文綺、銷金帳幔諸物。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongle the court sent the eunuch Yin Qing as envoy, granting gold-woven brocades, gilded curtains, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongle year 1 the eunuch Yin Qing was sent with gifts of gold-woven brocades and gilded hangings.

sentences.zh: 其地無王，亦不稱國，服屬暹羅，歲輸金四十兩為賦。

translations.literal: The place had no king and did not style itself a state; it was subject to Siam and paid forty taels of gold yearly as tax.
translations.idiomatic: It had no king and was not called a kingdom, but paid Siam forty taels of gold yearly in tribute.

sentences.zh: 慶至，宣示威德及招徠之意。

translations.literal: When Qing arrived he proclaimed imperial might and the intent to win allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Qing proclaimed the court's power and its wish to receive their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 其酋拜裡迷蘇剌大喜，遣使隨慶入朝貢方物，三年九月至京師。

translations.literal: The chieftain Parameswara was greatly pleased and sent envoys with Qing to court with local products; in the ninth month of the third year they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Parameswara rejoiced, sent envoys with Qing bearing tribute, and reached the capital in the ninth month of year 3.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，封為滿剌加國王，賜誥印、彩幣、襲衣、黃蓋，覆命慶往。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended this and enfeoffed him as king of Malacca, granting patent, seal, colored silks, investiture robes, and a yellow canopy, and again ordered Qing to go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enfeoffed him as king of Malacca, granting patent, seal, silks, robes, and a yellow canopy, and sent Qing back.

sentences.zh: 其使者言：「王慕義，願同中國列郡，歲效職貢，請封其山為一國之鎮。」

translations.literal: His envoys said: "The king admires righteousness and wishes to rank with the inner commanderies of China, offering yearly service and tribute; he asks that his mountain be enfeoffed as the guardian peak of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys said: "Our king wishes to be counted among China's inner districts, to offer yearly tribute, and to have his mountain enfeoffed as the kingdom's guardian peak.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 制碑文，勒山上，末綴以詩曰：「西南巨海中國通，輸天灌地億載同。

translations.literal: He composed an inscription and had it carved on the mountain, appending a poem that reads: "In the great sea of the southwest China is joined; heaven pours and earth irrigates, the same for a hundred million ages.
translations.idiomatic: He had an inscription cut on the mountain, ending with a poem: "In the southwest's vast sea we join with China; heaven and earth pour down, age on age the same.

sentences.zh: 洗日浴月光景融，雨崖露石草木濃。

translations.literal: Washing sun and bathing moon, light and radiance blend; rain cliffs and dewy stones, plants and trees grow thick.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon washed bright, light and shade mingled; cliffs wetted by rain, stones beaded with dew, vegetation lush.

sentences.zh: 金花寶鈿生青紅，有國於此民俗雍。

translations.literal: Golden flowers and jeweled inlays show green and red; here is a state whose folk live in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Gold flowers and jeweled filigree in green and red—a land whose people live in peace.

sentences.zh: 王好善義思朝宗，願比內郡依華風。

translations.literal: The king loves goodness and righteousness and thinks of paying court, wishing to be like the inner districts and follow Chinese ways.
translations.idiomatic: The king loves virtue and longs for court, wishing to follow Chinese custom like the inner provinces.

sentences.zh: 出入導從張蓋重，儀文裼襲禮虔恭。

translations.literal: Going out and in, guides and followers, umbrellas and canopies are weighty; ritual vestments and lined robes, ceremony reverent and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: His retinue goes forth with heavy state umbrellas; ritual dress and courteous ceremony show his reverence.

sentences.zh: 大書貞石表爾忠，爾國西山永鎮封。

translations.literal: Great characters on faithful stone declare your loyalty; your kingdom's western mountain is forever enfeoffed to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Great words on steadfast stone proclaim your loyalty; your western mountain is enfeoffed forever to guard the realm.

sentences.zh: 山君海伯翕扈從，皇考陟降在彼穹。

translations.literal: Mountain lords and sea dukes gather in attendance; the August Father ascends and descends in that vault of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain spirits and sea lords attend together; our August Ancestor watches from on high.

sentences.zh: 後天監視久彌隆，爾眾子孫萬福崇。」

translations.literal: Heaven above oversees long and ever more glorious; your multitudes and descendants, ten thousand blessings and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's gaze endures and grows brighter; may your people and heirs know ten thousand blessings.

sentences.zh: 慶等再至，其王益喜，禮待有加。

translations.literal: When Qing and the others came again, the king was still more pleased and treated them with added courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Qing returned, the king was still more delighted and honored them further.

sentences.zh: 五年九月遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year envoys were sent with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 5 envoys brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年，鄭和使其國，旋入貢。

translations.literal: The next year Zheng He was sent to their country, and they soon sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zheng He visited, and they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 九年，其王率妻子陪臣五百四十餘人來朝。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the king led his wife, children, and more than five hundred forty attending ministers to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the king came with wife, children, and over five hundred forty ministers.

sentences.zh: 抵近郊，命中官海壽、禮部郎中黃裳等宴勞，有司供張會同館。

translations.literal: When they neared the suburbs, the Emperor ordered the eunuch Hai Shou and Secretariat Director Huang Shang and others to feast and comfort them; the relevant offices supplied provisions at the Hostel for Tributary Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Near the capital the court sent Hai Shou and Huang Shang to entertain them and lodged them at the tributary hostel.

sentences.zh: 入朝奉天殿，帝親宴之，妃以下宴他所。

translations.literal: They entered court at Fengtian Hall; the Emperor personally feasted them, and the consort and others were feasted elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: They were received at Fengtian Hall; the emperor feasted the king himself and the consort's party elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 光祿日致牲牢上尊，賜王金繡龍衣二襲、麒麟衣一襲，金銀器、帷幔衾衤周悉具，妃以下皆有賜。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Entertainments daily sent sacrificial animals and fine wine; the king was granted two suits of gold-embroidered dragon robes and one of qilin robe, gold and silver vessels, curtains, quilts, and bedding in full, and the consort and those below all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Daily they received meat and wine; the king got dragon robes, qilin robes, gold and silver ware, hangings, and bedding, and the consort's party gifts in proportion.

sentences.zh: 將歸，賜王玉帶、儀仗、鞍馬，賜妃冠服。

translations.literal: When they were about to return, the king was granted a jade belt, ceremonial guards, and saddle and horse, and the consort was granted cap and robes.
translations.idiomatic: On departure the king received a jade belt, guards, and mount; the consort received cap and robes.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，賜宴奉天門，再賜玉帶、儀仗、鞍馬、黃金百、白金五百、鈔四十萬貫、錢二千六百貫、錦綺紗羅三百匹、帛千匹、渾金文綺二、金織通袖膝襕二；

translations.literal: Before they left, a feast was given at Fengtian Gate; they were again granted jade belt, guards, saddle and horse, one hundred taels of gold, five hundred of white gold, four hundred thousand strings of paper money, two thousand six hundred strings of cash, three hundred bolts of brocade, gauze, and silk, one thousand bolts of plain silk, two bolts of pure gold brocade, and two gold-woven full-sleeve knee-length robes;
translations.idiomatic: At a farewell feast they received again belt, guards, horses, a hundred taels of gold, five hundred of silver, forty myriads of paper money, cash, silks, and gold-woven robes;

sentences.zh: 妃及子侄陪臣以下，宴賜有差。

translations.literal: the consort, sons, nephews, and attending ministers below all received feasts and gifts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: the consort, kin, and ministers were feasted and rewarded in due measure.

sentences.zh: 禮官餞於龍江驛，復賜宴龍潭驛。

translations.literal: The ritual officials saw them off at Longjiang Post and again gave a feast at Longtan Post.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites feasted them at Longjiang and Longtan posts on the way out.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，其侄入謝。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year his nephew came to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year 10 his nephew came to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 及辭歸，命中官甘泉偕往，旋又入貢。

translations.literal: When they took leave to return, the eunuch Gan Quan was ordered to go with them; they soon sent tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the eunuch Gan Quan escorted them; they sent tribute again soon after.

sentences.zh: 十二年，王子母干撒於的兒沙來朝，告其父訃。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the prince's mother Gan Sa-yu-di-er-sha came to court to announce the king's death.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 the prince's mother came to announce the king's death.

sentences.zh: 即命襲封，賜金幣。

translations.literal: He was at once ordered to succeed to the enfeoffment and was granted gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was immediately confirmed as king and granted gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 嗣後，或連歲，或間歲入貢以為常。

translations.literal: Thereafter they sent tribute every year or every other year as a rule.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute came yearly or every other year as a matter of course.

sentences.zh: 十七年，王率妻子陪臣來朝謝恩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the king led wife, children, and ministers to court to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 the king came with family and ministers to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 及辭歸，訴暹羅見侵狀。

translations.literal: When they took leave to return they reported how Siam had encroached upon them.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving they complained of invasion by Siam.

sentences.zh: 帝為賜敕諭暹羅，暹羅乃奉詔。

translations.literal: The Emperor accordingly granted an edict admonishing Siam, and Siam then obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an edict rebuking Siam, and Siam obeyed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，西里麻哈剌以父沒嗣位，率妻子陪臣來朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Sri Maharaja succeeded on his father's death and led wife, children, and ministers to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 Sri Maharaja succeeded and came with family and ministers.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年遣使者來言：「暹羅謀侵本國，王欲入朝，懼為所阻，欲奏聞，無能書者，令臣三人附蘇門答剌貢舟入訴。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande envoys came saying: "Siam plots to invade our country; the king wishes to come to court but fears being blocked and wishes to memorialize but has no one who can write; he has sent us three men on Sulu's tribute ship to enter a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 6 envoys said: "Siam threatens us; our king wishes to come to court but fears obstruction, and having no scribe sends us three on Sulu's ship to plead.

sentences.zh: 帝命附鄭和舟歸國，因令和齎敕諭暹羅，責以輯睦鄰封，毋違朝命。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered them to return on Zheng He's fleet and had He carry an edict rebuking Siam, charging it to live in harmony with neighboring states and not defy the court's command.
translations.idiomatic: They were sent back on Zheng He's fleet with an edict rebuking Siam to keep peace with its neighbors.

sentences.zh: 初，三人至，無貢物，禮官言例不當賞。

translations.literal: At first when the three men arrived they brought no tribute; the ritual officials said that by precedent they should not be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: When the three arrived without tribute, the Board of Rites said rewards were not due by precedent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遠人越數萬里來醞不平，豈可無賜。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Men from afar have crossed tens of thousands of li to bring word of injustice—how can we give them nothing?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "They have crossed oceans to report injustice—how can we send them away empty-handed?

sentences.zh: 遂賜襲衣、彩幣，如貢使例。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were granted investiture robes and colored silks as for tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted robes and silks as if they were tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 八年，王率妻子陪臣來朝。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the king led wife, children, and ministers to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the king came again with family and ministers.

sentences.zh: 抵南京，天已寒，命俟春和北上，別遣人齎敕勞賜王及妃。

translations.literal: They reached Nanjing when the weather was already cold; he was ordered to wait until spring before going north, and others were separately sent with an edict to comfort and reward the king and consort.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Nanjing in cold weather and were told to wait for spring; envoys were sent ahead with gifts for king and consort.

sentences.zh: 洎入朝，宴賚如禮。

translations.literal: When they entered court, feasts and gifts followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At court they were feasted and rewarded according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 及還，有司為治舟。

translations.literal: When they returned, the relevant offices prepared boats for them.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the offices fitted out ships.

sentences.zh: 王復遣其弟貢駝馬方物。

translations.literal: The king again sent his younger brother with tribute of camels, horses, and local products.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent his brother with camels, horses, and local goods.

sentences.zh: 時英宗已嗣位，而王猶在廣東。

translations.literal: By then Emperor Yingzong had already succeeded, yet the king was still in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong had already succeeded, but the king was still in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 賜敕獎王，命守臣送還國。

translations.literal: An edict was granted praising the king and ordering the guarding officials to send him home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him and ordered local officials to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 因遣古裡、真臘等十一國使臣，附載偕還。

translations.literal: Envoys from eleven states including Calicut and Cambodia were also sent to return on the same ships.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Calicut, Cambodia, and nine other states sailed back with him.

sentences.zh: 正統十年，其使者請賜王息力八密息瓦兒丟八沙護國敕書及蟒服、傘蓋，以鎮服國人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong their envoys asked that the king be granted a patent of investiture for the realm and python robes and parasol and canopy to awe the people of the country.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year 10 envoys asked for investiture patents, python robes, and state umbrellas to overawe the realm.

sentences.zh: 又言：「王欲親詣闕下，從人多，乞賜一巨舟，以便遠涉。」

translations.literal: They also said: "The king wishes to come to court in person; his retinue is large, and we beg one great ship for the long voyage.
translations.idiomatic: They also said the king wished to come in person with a large retinue and begged a great ship for the voyage.

sentences.zh: 帝悉從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented to all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted everything.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年，速魯檀無答佛哪沙貢馬及方物，請封為王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai Sultan Muhammad Shah presented horses and local products and asked to be enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai year 6 Sultan Muhammad Shah sent horses and goods and asked to be made king.

sentences.zh: 詔給事中王暉往。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Supervising Secretary Wang Hui to go.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Hui was ordered to go.

sentences.zh: 已，復入貢，言所賜冠帶毀於火。

translations.literal: Later they sent tribute again, saying the granted cap and belt had been destroyed by fire.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute again, saying the granted cap and belt had burned.

sentences.zh: 命制皮弁服、紅羅常服及犀帶紗帽予之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be given a leather cap-robe set, red-silk regular dress, rhinoceros-horn belt, and gauze hat.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered new leather court dress, red robes, rhinoceros belt, and gauze hat made for him.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，王子蘇丹芒速沙遣使入貢，命給事中陳嘉猷等往封之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun the prince Sultan Mansur Shah sent envoys with tribute; Supervising Secretary Chen Jiayou and others were ordered to go and enfeoff him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun year 3 Prince Sultan Mansur Shah sent tribute; Chen Jiayou was sent to enfeoff him.

sentences.zh: 越二年，禮官言：「嘉猷等浮海二日，至烏豬洋，遇颶風，舟壞，飄六日至清瀾守禦所獲救。

translations.literal: Two years later the ritual officials said: "Jiayou and the others sailed two days and reached Wuzhu Yang; they met a typhoon, the boat was wrecked, and after drifting six days they were rescued at Qinglan Defense Station.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later officials reported Chen Jiayou's ship was wrecked in a typhoon off Wuzhu Yang and the party rescued after six days adrift.

sentences.zh: 敕書無失，諸賜物悉沾水。

translations.literal: The edict was not lost, but all the gifts were soaked.
translations.idiomatic: The patent was saved but the gifts were soaked.

sentences.zh: 乞重給，令使臣復往。」

translations.literal: They begged that gifts be issued again and the envoys be sent once more.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that gifts be reissued and the mission sent again.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 成化十年，給事中陳峻冊封佔城王，遇安南兵據佔城不得入，以所齎物至滿剌加，諭其王入貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua Supervising Secretary Chen Jun was sent to enfeoff the king of Champa but, meeting Annamese troops occupying Champa, could not enter; he took the goods he carried to Malacca and urged its king to send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 10 Chen Jun, bound to enfeoff Champa, found Annam blocking the way and went instead to Malacca to urge tribute.

sentences.zh: 其使者至，帝喜，賜敕嘉獎。

translations.literal: When their envoys arrived the Emperor was pleased and granted an edict of praise and reward.
translations.idiomatic: When Malacca's envoys came, the emperor was pleased and sent a commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 十七年九月，貢使言：「成化五年，貢使還，飄抵安南境，多被殺，余黥為奴，幼者加宮刑。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventeenth year tribute envoys said: "In the fifth year of Chenghua, when tribute envoys returned, they were blown to Annamese territory; many were killed, the rest branded as slaves, and the young were given palace castration.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 17 envoys said that in Chenghua year 5 returning envoys were driven to Annam, many killed, survivors enslaved, boys castrated.

sentences.zh: 今已據佔城地，又欲吞本國。

translations.literal: Now they have seized Champa's territory and also wish to swallow our country.
translations.idiomatic: Now they hold Champa and seek to swallow our kingdom too.

sentences.zh: 本國以皆為王臣，未敢與戰。」

translations.literal: Our country, being subjects of the Son of Heaven, has not dared to fight.
translations.idiomatic: We are the Son of Heaven's subjects and have not dared to fight.

sentences.zh: 適安南貢使亦至，滿剌加使臣請與廷辨。

translations.literal: Just then Annamese tribute envoys also arrived, and the Malacca envoys asked to debate them at court.
translations.idiomatic: Annam's envoys arrived at the same time, and Malacca asked for a court debate.

sentences.zh: 兵部言事屬既往，不足深較。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War said the matter belonged to the past and was not worth pressing deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War said the affair was past and not worth pursuing.

sentences.zh: 帝乃因安南使還，敕責其王，並諭滿剌加，安南復侵陵，即整兵待戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent back the Annamese envoys with an edict rebuking their king, and also instructed Malacca that if Annam again encroached, it should ready troops and await battle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Annam's king by returning envoys with an edict and told Malacca to prepare for war if Annam attacked again.

sentences.zh: 尋遣給事中林榮、行人黃乾亨冊封王子馬哈木沙為王。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Supervising Secretary Lin Rong and Courier Huang Qianheng were sent to enfeoff the prince Mahmud Shah as king.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Lin Rong and Huang Qianheng were sent to enfeoff Prince Mahmud Shah.

sentences.zh: 二人溺死，贈官賜祭，予廕，恤其家，余敕有司海濱招魂祭，亦恤其家。

translations.literal: The two men drowned; offices were granted posthumously, sacrifices bestowed, hereditary privilege given their families, and the rest were ordered to conduct soul-recalling rites on the seashore and comfort their families as well.
translations.idiomatic: Both drowned; posthumous offices, sacrifices, and enfeoffment benefits were granted their families, and others were ordered to conduct seaside rites for their souls.

sentences.zh: 復遣給事中張晟、行人左輔往。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Sheng and Courier Zuo Fu were again sent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng and Courier Zuo Fu were sent again.

sentences.zh: 晟卒於廣東，命守臣擇一官為輔副，以終封事。

translations.literal: Sheng died in Guangdong; the guarding officials were ordered to choose one officer as Fu's deputy to complete the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng died in Guangdong; local officials chose a deputy for Zuo Fu to finish the mission.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，使臣端亞智等入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde envoys Tuan Yazhi and others entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 3 envoys led by Tuan Yazhi brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 其通事亞劉，本江西萬安人蕭明舉，負罪逃入其國，賂大通事王永、序班張字，謀往浡泥索寶。

translations.literal: Their interpreter Ya Liu was originally Xiao Mingju of Wan'an in Jiangxi, who had fled there for a crime; he bribed the chief interpreter Wang Yong and clerk Zhang Yu, plotting to go to Brunei to seek treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreter Ya Liu was the fugitive Jiangxi man Xiao Mingju, who bribed chief interpreter Wang Yong and clerk Zhang Yu to seek treasure in Brunei.

sentences.zh: 而禮部吏侯永等亦受賂，偽為符印，擾郵傳。

translations.literal: Clerk Hou Yong of the Ministry of Rites also took bribes and forged seals and tallies, disturbing the courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites clerk Hou Yong also took bribes and forged seals, disrupting the courier system.

sentences.zh: 還至廣東，明舉與端亞智輩爭言，遂與同事彭萬春等劫殺之，盡取其財物。

translations.literal: When they returned to Guangdong, Mingju and Tuan Yazhi and the others quarreled, and together with their colleague Peng Wanchun and others they robbed and killed them, taking all their goods.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Guangdong, Mingju quarreled with Tuan Yazhi's party; he and Peng Wanchun murdered them and seized their goods.

sentences.zh: 事覺，逮入京。

translations.literal: When the affair was discovered they were arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The crime discovered, they were brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明舉凌遲，萬春等斬，王永減死罰米三百石，與張字、侯永並戍邊，尚書白鉞以下皆議罰。

translations.literal: Mingju was executed by slicing; Wanchun and others were beheaded; Wang Yong's death sentence was commuted to a fine of three hundred piculs of rice; he, Zhang Yu, and Hou Yong were all banished to the frontier; the Minister Bai Yue and those below were all penalized by deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Mingju suffered death by slicing; Wanchun and others were beheaded; Wang Yong paid a rice fine in lieu of death; Zhang Yu and Hou Yong were exiled; Minister Bai Yue and others were punished.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾因此罪江西人，減其解額五十名，仕者不得任京職。

translations.literal: Liu Jin used this crime to condemn Jiangxi men, reducing their quota of presented scholars by fifty and barring officeholders from capital posts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin used the case to penalize Jiangxi, cutting fifty places from its quota and barring its officials from capital posts.

sentences.zh: 後佛郎機強，舉兵侵奪其地，王蘇端媽末出奔，遣使告難。

translations.literal: Later the Portuguese grew strong, raised troops, and seized its territory; King Su-duan-ma-mo fled abroad and sent envoys to report the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Portuguese invaded; King Su-duan-ma-mo fled and sent envoys begging aid.

sentences.zh: 時世宗嗣位，敕責佛郎機，令還其故土。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shizong had just succeeded and issued an edict rebuking the Portuguese, ordering them to restore the former territory.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor Shizong rebuked Portugal and ordered restoration of Malacca's land.

sentences.zh: 諭暹羅諸國王以救災恤鄰之義，迄無應者，滿剌加竟為所滅。

translations.literal: He instructed the kings of Siam and other states in the duty of aiding neighbors in disaster, but in the end none responded, and Malacca was finally destroyed by them.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Siam and others to aid a neighbor in distress, but none responded and Malacca was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 時佛郎機亦遣使朝貢請封，抵廣東，守臣以其國素不列《王會》，羈其使以聞。

translations.literal: At that time the Portuguese also sent envoys to court to request enfeoffment; they reached Guangdong, and the guarding officials, since their state had never been listed in the royal assembly accounts, detained the envoys and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Portugal also sent envoys seeking enfeoffment; Guangdong officials, finding them unlisted in court registers, detained them and reported upward.

sentences.zh: 詔予方物之直遣歸，後改名麻六甲雲。

translations.literal: An edict granted the value of the tribute goods and sent them home; later the name was changed to Majia-liujia.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid for their goods and sent them home; the place was later called Majia-liujia.

sentences.zh: 滿剌加所貢物有瑪瑙、珍珠、玳瑁、珊瑚樹、鶴頂、金母鶴頂、瑣服、白苾布、西洋布、撒哈剌、犀角、象牙、黑熊、黑猿、白麂、火雞、鸚鵡、片腦、薔薇露、蘇合油、梔子花、烏爹泥、沉香、速香、金銀香、阿魏之屬。

translations.literal: Tribute products of Malacca included agate, pearls, tortoiseshell, coral trees, hornbill casques, gold-inlaid hornbill casques, filigree garments, white cotton cloth, Western cloth, sa-ha-la, rhinoceros horn, ivory, black bears, black gibbons, white deer, turkeys, parrots, camphor flakes, rose dew, storax oil, gardenia flowers, udambari, aloeswood, gharuwood, gold and silver incense, asafoetida, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Malacca's tribute included agate, pearls, tortoiseshell, coral, hornbill casques, filigree dress, cotton and Western cloths, rhinoceros horn, ivory, rare animals, camphor, rose water, storax, gardenia, udambari, aloeswood, gharuwood, and similar goods.

sentences.zh: 有山出泉流為溪，土人淘沙取錫煎成塊曰斗錫。

translations.literal: There is a mountain from which springs flow in streams; the natives pan the sand for tin and smelt it into ingots called dou tin.
translations.idiomatic: A mountain sends out streams; locals pan sand for tin and cast it into ingots called dou tin.

sentences.zh: 田瘠少收，民皆淘沙捕魚為業。

translations.literal: The fields are poor and harvests small; the people all pan sand and catch fish for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Soil is thin and yields little; people live by panning sand and fishing.

sentences.zh: 氣候朝熱暮寒。

translations.literal: The climate is hot in the morning and cold in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Mornings are hot and evenings cool.

sentences.zh: 男女椎髻，身體黝黑，間有白者，唐人種也。

translations.literal: Men and women wear their hair in topknots; their bodies are dark, though some are fair—these are of Chinese descent.
translations.idiomatic: People wear topknots and dark skin, though some fair-skinned folk are of Chinese stock.

sentences.zh: 俗淳厚，市道頗平。

translations.literal: Customs are simple and honest, and market dealings are fairly equitable.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were honest and markets fairly conducted.

sentences.zh: 自為佛郎機所破，其風頓殊。

translations.literal: Since it was broken by the Portuguese, its ways changed abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: After the Portuguese conquest its ways changed sharply.

sentences.zh: 商舶稀至，多直詣蘇門答剌。

translations.literal: Trading ships rarely came, and most went straight to Sumatra.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant fleets seldom called; most sailed straight for Sumatra.

sentences.zh: 然必取道其國，率被邀劫，海路幾斷。

translations.literal: Yet they had to pass through its territory and were often waylaid, so the sea route was nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ships had to pass its waters and were often robbed, nearly severing the route.

sentences.zh: 其自販於中國者，則直達廣東香山澳，接跡不絕雲。

translations.literal: Those who traded on their own with China went straight to Xiangshan Ao in Guangdong, and their arrivals followed one after another without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Private traders with China went directly to Xiangshan Ao in Guangdong in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 蘇門答剌

translations.literal: Sumatra
translations.idiomatic: Sumatra

sentences.zh: 蘇門答剌，在滿剌加之西。

translations.literal: Sumatra lies west of Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: Sumatra lies west of Malacca.

sentences.zh: 順風九晝夜可至。

translations.literal: With a fair wind one can reach it in nine days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: With fair winds it is nine days and nights' sail.

sentences.zh: 或言即漢條枝，唐波斯、大食二國地，西洋要會也。

translations.literal: Some say it is Han's Tiaozhi and Tang's Persia and Dashi lands—the great meeting place of the Western Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Some identify it with Han Tiaozhi and Tang Persia and Arabia—the crossroads of the Western Ocean.

sentences.zh: 成祖初，遣使以即位詔諭其國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengzu's reign envoys were sent with the accession edict to instruct the country.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chengzu's reign envoys carried the accession edict there.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年遣副使聞良輔、行人甯善賜其酋織金文綺、絨錦、紗羅招徠之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle Deputy Envoy Wen Liangfu and Courier Ning Shan were sent to grant the chieftain gold-woven brocades, pile velvets, gauze, and silk to win allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2 Wen Liangfu and Ning Shan were sent with brocades and silks to win allegiance.

sentences.zh: 中官尹慶使爪哇，便道復使其國。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yin Qing, sent to Java, went by the way of that country and again instructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Yin Qing, bound for Java, called there again on the way.

sentences.zh: 三年，鄭和下西洋，復有賜。

translations.literal: In the third year Zheng He went to the Western Ocean and gifts were again bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Zheng He's voyage brought further gifts.

sentences.zh: 和未至，其酋宰奴裡阿必丁已遣使隨慶入朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: Before He arrived, the chieftain Zainal Abidin had already sent envoys with Qing to court with local products.
translations.idiomatic: Before He arrived, Chief Zainal Abidin had already sent envoys with Qing bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔封為蘇門答剌國王，賜印誥、彩幣、襲衣。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed him as king of Sumatra, granting seal, patent, colored silks, and investiture robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed king of Sumatra with seal, patent, silks, and robes.

sentences.zh: 遂比年入貢，終成祖世不絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute came yearly, and it did not cease throughout Chengzu's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute then came yearly without break through Chengzu's reign.

sentences.zh: 鄭和凡三使其國。

translations.literal: Zheng He in all made three missions to that country.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He visited the country three times.

sentences.zh: 先是，其王之父與鄰國花面王戰，中矢死。

translations.literal: Earlier, this king's father had fought with the neighboring Flower-Face King and died from an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: The present king's father had died fighting the neighboring Flower-Face King.

sentences.zh: 王子年幼，王妻號於眾曰：「孰能為我報仇者，我以為夫，與共國事。」

translations.literal: The prince was young; the king's wife cried out to the multitude: "Whoever can avenge me, I will take as husband and share the rule of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was young; the queen proclaimed: "Whoever avenges my husband I will marry and share the realm.

sentences.zh: 有漁翁聞之，率國人往擊，馘其王而還。

translations.literal: A fisherman heard this, led the people to attack, cut off the enemy king's head, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: A fisherman led the people out, slew the enemy king, and returned.

sentences.zh: 王妻遂與之合，稱為老王。

translations.literal: The king's wife then joined with him and called him the Old King.
translations.idiomatic: The queen married him and called him the Old King.

sentences.zh: 既而王子年長，潛與部領謀，殺老王而襲其位。

translations.literal: When the prince grew older he secretly plotted with tribal leaders, killed the Old King, and seized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince grew up he plotted with chiefs, killed the Old King, and seized power.

sentences.zh: 老王弟蘇干剌逃山中，連年率眾侵擾。

translations.literal: The Old King's younger brother Sekandar fled to the mountains and for years led bands to raid and harass.
translations.idiomatic: The Old King's brother Sekandar fled to the hills and raided for years.

sentences.zh: 十三年，和復至其國，蘇干剌以頒賜不及己，怒，統數萬人邀擊。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year He again reached the country; Sekandar, because distributions had not reached him, was angry and led tens of thousands to intercept and attack.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 He returned; Sekandar, angry at being passed over in gifts, attacked with tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 和勒部卒及國人御之，大破賊眾，追至南渤利國，俘以歸。

translations.literal: He marshaled his troops and the people of the country to resist, greatly defeated the rebel host, pursued them to Lamuri, and brought the captive back.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied troops and locals, routed the rebels, pursued them to Lamuri, and brought Sekandar back captive.

sentences.zh: 其王遣使入謝。

translations.literal: The king sent envoys to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent envoys to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年遣使入賀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande envoys were sent to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 1 envoys came with congratulations.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝以外蕃貢使多不至，遣和及王景弘遍歷諸國，頒詔曰：「朕恭膺天命，祗承太祖高皇帝、太宗文皇帝、仁宗昭皇帝大統，君臨萬邦，體祖宗之至仁，普輯寧於庶類。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because many foreign tribute missions had not come, the Emperor sent He and Wang Jinghong to go through all the states, proclaiming an edict: "I respectfully received Heaven's mandate and succeed to the great design of the Grand Ancestor, the Literary Emperor, and the Accomplished Emperor, ruling the myriad regions and embodying the utmost benevolence of the ancestors to bring peace to all kinds.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, with many tributaries absent, the emperor sent He and Wang Jinghong with an edict proclaiming his succession and benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 已大赦天下，紀元宣德。

translations.literal: A great amnesty has been proclaimed for the empire and the reign title is fixed as Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: A great amnesty has been proclaimed and the era named Xuande.

sentences.zh: 爾諸蕃國，遠在海外，未有聞知。

translations.literal: Your various barbarian states, far overseas, have not yet heard of this.
translations.idiomatic: You overseas realms have not yet heard.

sentences.zh: 茲遣太監鄭和、王景弘等齎詔往諭，其各敬天道，撫人民，共享太平之福。」

translations.literal: Now the eunuch Zheng He, Wang Jinghong, and others are sent bearing edicts to instruct you; each of you should revere Heaven's way, comfort the people, and share the blessings of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He and Wang Jinghong carry edicts: revere Heaven, comfort your people, and share great peace.

sentences.zh: 凡歷二十餘國，蘇門答剌與焉。

translations.literal: In all more than twenty states were visited, and Sumatra was among them."
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty states were visited, Sumatra among them.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使入貢者再。

translations.literal: The next year envoys came with tribute twice.
translations.idiomatic: The next year tribute envoys came twice.

sentences.zh: 八年貢麒麟。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they presented a qilin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 they presented a qilin.

sentences.zh: 九年，王弟哈利之漢來朝，卒於京。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the king's younger brother Halizhihan came to court and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the king's brother Halizhihan came to court and died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝憫之，贈鴻臚少卿，賜誥，有司治喪葬，置守冢戶。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied him, granted him posthumous rank as Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, bestowed a patent, and ordered the relevant offices to conduct funeral rites and set up tomb-guard households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied him, granted posthumous rank, a patent, funeral rites, and tomb-guard households.

sentences.zh: 時景弘再使其國，王遣弟哈尼者罕隨入朝。

translations.literal: At that time Jinghong was again sent to their country, and the king sent his younger brother Hanizhehan to come to court with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinghong was sent again, the king's brother Hanizhehan came with him.

sentences.zh: 明年至，言王老不能治事，請傳位於子。

translations.literal: The next year when he arrived he said the old king could no longer govern and asked that the succession pass to his son.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he reported the old king could not rule and asked succession for the son.

sentences.zh: 乃封其子阿卜賽亦的為國王，自是貢使漸稀。

translations.literal: His son Abusaid was then enfeoffed as king, and thereafter tribute missions grew rare.
translations.idiomatic: Son Abusaid was enfeoffed; thereafter tribute grew infrequent.

sentences.zh: 成化二十二年，其使者至廣東，有司驗無印信勘合，乃藏其表於庫，卻還其使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Chenghua their envoys reached Guangdong; the relevant offices found no seal or tally-slips and therefore stored their memorial in the treasury and sent the envoys back.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua year 22 envoys reached Guangdong without seal or tallies; officials stored their memorial and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 別遣番人輸貢物京師，稍有給賜。

translations.literal: They separately sent foreigners to present tribute goods to the capital and were somewhat rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Others sent tribute goods to the capital and received modest rewards.

sentences.zh: 自後貢使不至。

translations.literal: After that tribute envoys did not come.
translations.idiomatic: After that no tribute envoys came.

sentences.zh: 迨萬曆間，國兩易姓。

translations.literal: By the Wanli period the ruling house had twice changed surname.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the throne changed hands twice.

sentences.zh: 其時為王者，人奴也。

translations.literal: The man who was then king had been a slave.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning king had once been a slave.

sentences.zh: 奴之主為國大臣，握兵柄。

translations.literal: The slave's master was a great minister of state who held military power.
translations.idiomatic: His master was a great minister who held the army.

sentences.zh: 奴桀黠，主使牧象，象肥。

translations.literal: The slave was fierce and cunning; his master had him herd elephants, and the elephants grew fat.
translations.idiomatic: The slave was clever and fierce; his master set him to tend elephants until they grew fat.

sentences.zh: 俾監魚稅，日以大魚奉其主。

translations.literal: He was made to supervise the fish tax and daily presented large fish to his master.
translations.idiomatic: He was put over the fish tax and daily sent large fish to his master.

sentences.zh: 主大喜，俾給事左右。

translations.literal: The master was greatly pleased and had him serve at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The master was pleased and kept him in attendance.

sentences.zh: 一日隨主入朝，見王尊嚴若神，主鞠躬惟謹，出謂主曰：「主何恭之甚？」

translations.literal: One day he followed his master into court and saw the king revered as a god; his master bowed with utmost care. Going out he said to his master: "Why such great deference?
translations.idiomatic: One day in court he saw the king honored like a god while his master bowed low; outside he asked why such deference.

sentences.zh: 主曰：「彼王也，焉敢抗。」

translations.literal: The master said: "That is the king—how would I dare resist?"
translations.idiomatic: The master said: "He is the king—how dare I resist?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「主第不欲王爾，欲之，主即王矣。」

translations.literal: He said: "If my lord does not wish to be king, that is one thing; if you wish it, my lord would be king."
translations.idiomatic: The slave said: "If you do not want to be king, that is your choice; if you want it, you can be king."

sentences.zh: 主詫，叱退之。

translations.literal: The master was startled and rebuked him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The master was shocked and drove him away.

sentences.zh: 他日又進曰：「王左右侍衛少，主擁重兵出鎮，必入辭，請以奴從。

translations.literal: Another day he advanced again, saying: "The king has few guards at his side; my lord holds heavy troops and goes out to command—when you enter to take leave, ask to bring me as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later he urged: "The king has few guards; you command great forces—bring me when you take leave of court.

sentences.zh: 主言有機事，乞屏左右，王必不疑。

translations.literal: Say there is a confidential matter and beg to dismiss those present—the king will surely not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: Plead confidential business and dismiss attendants—the king will not suspect.

sentences.zh: 奴乘間剌殺之，奉主為王，猶反掌耳。」

translations.literal: I will seize the moment to stab and kill him, install my lord as king—it is like turning the hand over.
translations.idiomatic: I will stab the king and make you king—it is as easy as turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 主從之，奴果殺王，大呼曰：「王不道，吾殺之。

translations.literal: The master consented; the slave indeed killed the king and cried out loudly: "The king was without the Way—I have killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The master agreed; the slave killed the king and shouted that the king was unjust.

sentences.zh: 吾主即王矣。

translations.literal: My lord is now king.
translations.idiomatic: My lord is king now.

sentences.zh: 敢異議者，齒此刃！」

translations.literal: Whoever dares disagree, taste this blade!"
translations.idiomatic: Whoever objects, taste this blade!

sentences.zh: 眾懾服不敢動，其主遂篡位，任奴為心腹，委以兵柄。

translations.literal: The multitude were cowed and dared not move; his master then usurped the throne, appointed the slave as his trusted confidant, and entrusted him with military power.
translations.idiomatic: All were cowed; the master usurped the throne and gave the slave command of the army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，奴復殺主而代之。

translations.literal: Before long the slave again killed his master and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the slave killed his master and took the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 乃大為防衛，拓其宮，建六門，不得闌入，雖勳貴不得帶刀上殿。
