translations.literal: He then greatly strengthened defenses, enlarged the palace, built six gates, and forbade unauthorized entry; even meritorious nobles could not enter the hall bearing swords.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified the palace with six gates, barred casual entry, and forbade even nobles swords in hall.

sentences.zh: 出乘象，象駕亭而帷其外，如是者百餘，俾人莫測王所在。

translations.literal: Going out he rode an elephant; the elephant bore a pavilion curtained outside—more than a hundred such—so that none could know where the king was.
translations.idiomatic: He rode out on elephants under curtained pavilions—over a hundred—so none knew where the king was.

sentences.zh: 其國俗頗淳，出言柔媚，惟王好殺。

translations.literal: The customs of the country were rather simple; speech was gentle and ingratiating, but the king loved killing.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were mild and speech soft, but the king loved bloodshed.

sentences.zh: 歲殺十餘人，取其血浴身，謂可除疾。

translations.literal: Each year he killed more than ten men and bathed his body in their blood, saying it could remove illness.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he killed a dozen men and bathed in their blood, claiming it cured disease.

sentences.zh: 貢物有寶石、瑪絜、水晶、石青、回回青、善馬、犀牛、龍涎香、沉香、速香、木香、丁香、降真香、刀、弓、錫、鎖服、胡椒、蘇木、硫黃之屬。

translations.literal: Tribute products included gems, carnelian, crystal, azurite, Muslim blue, fine horses, rhinoceroses, ambergris, aloeswood, gharuwood, eaglewood, cloves, eaglewood incense, swords, bows, tin, chain-mail garments, pepper, sappanwood, sulfur, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included gems, carnelian, crystal, pigments, fine horses, rhinoceros, ambergris, aloeswoods, cloves, arms, tin, armor, pepper, sappanwood, sulfur, and the like.

sentences.zh: 貨舶至，貿易稱平。

translations.literal: When merchant ships arrived, trade was said to be fair.
translations.idiomatic: When merchant fleets came, trade was reckoned fair.

sentences.zh: 地本瘠，無麥有禾，禾一歲二稔。

translations.literal: The land was originally poor; there was no wheat but there was rice, and rice yielded two crops a year.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was barren—no wheat, but rice twice a year.

sentences.zh: 四方商賈輻輳。

translations.literal: Merchants from the four quarters gathered thickly.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants from every quarter thronged there.

sentences.zh: 華人往者，以地遠價高，獲利倍他國。

translations.literal: Chinese who went there, because the distance made prices high, gained profits several times those of other countries.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese traders, because of the distance and high prices, profited several times more than elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 其氣候朝如夏，墓各秋，夏有瘴氣。

translations.literal: The climate was like summer in the morning and like autumn at dusk; in summer there was miasma.
translations.idiomatic: Mornings were summery and evenings autumnal; summer brought miasma.

sentences.zh: 婦人裸體，惟腰圍一布。

translations.literal: Women went naked, wearing only a cloth about the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Women went bare except for a waist cloth.

sentences.zh: 其他風俗類滿剌加。

translations.literal: Other customs resembled those of Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: Other customs resembled Malacca's.

sentences.zh: 篡弒後，易國名曰啞齊。

translations.literal: After the usurpation the state's name was changed to Aceh.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurpation the realm was renamed Aceh.

sentences.zh: 須文達那

translations.literal: Lamuri
translations.idiomatic: Lamuri

sentences.zh: 須文達那，洪武十六年，國王殊旦麻勒兀達朌遣使俺八兒來朝，貢馬二匹，幼苾布十五匹，隔著布、入的力布各二匹，花滿直地二，番綿紬直地二，兜羅綿二斤，撒剌八二個，幼賴革著一個，撒哈剌一個，及薔薇水、沉香、降香、速香諸物。

translations.literal: Lamuri: in the sixteenth year of Hongwu its king Sudarmauludin sent the envoy Aba'er to court with tribute of two horses, fifteen bolts of young cotton cloth, two bolts each of ge cloth and indigo cloth, two pieces of patterned full-width cloth, two of fine-patterned silk, two catties of tulle cotton, two sa-la-ba, one young deerskin garment, one sa-ha-la, and rose water, aloeswood, eaglewood, gharuwood, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 16 King Sudarmauludin sent Aba'er with horses, cottons, silks, and aromatics.

sentences.zh: 命賜王《大統歷》、綺羅、寶鈔，使臣襲衣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to grant the king the Comprehensive Calendar, brocades and gauzes, and treasure notes, and investiture robes to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted the king the calendar, silks, paper money, and robes to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 或言須文達那即蘇門答剌，洪武時所更，然其貢物與王之名皆不同，無可考。

translations.literal: Some say Lamuri is Sumatra under the name changed in Hongwu, yet its tribute goods and the king's name are all different and cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Lamuri is Sumatra renamed in Hongwu, but goods and royal names differ and cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿，地近浡泥、阇婆。

translations.literal: Sulu lies near Brunei and Java.
translations.idiomatic: The Sulu Archipelago lies near Brunei and Java.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，發兵侵浡泥，大獲，以阇婆援兵至，乃還。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Hongwu it sent troops to invade Brunei, gaining a great booty, but when Javanese relief troops arrived it returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu it invaded Brunei with great gain but withdrew when Java sent aid.

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年，其國東王巴都葛叭哈剌、西王麻哈剌叱葛剌麻丁、峒王妻叭都葛巴剌卜並率其家屬頭目凡三百四十餘人，浮海朝貢，進金鏤表文，獻珍珠、寶石、玳瑁諸物。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yongle the Eastern King Paduka Pahala, the Western King Maharajah Kamal ud-Din, and the Cave King Paduka Patulap, together leading more than three hundred forty of their families and chiefs, crossed the sea to court, presenting a gold-inlaid memorial and pearls, gems, tortoiseshell, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 15 the three Sulu kings came with over three hundred forty kin and chiefs, bearing a gold-inlaid memorial and gems.

sentences.zh: 禮之若滿剌加，尋並封為國王。

translations.literal: They were treated as Malacca had been, and shortly all three were enfeoffed as kings.
translations.idiomatic: They were honored like Malacca and all three were enfeoffed as kings.

sentences.zh: 賜印誥、襲衣、冠帶及鞍馬、儀仗器物，其從者亦賜冠帶有差。

translations.literal: Seals, patents, investiture robes, caps and belts, saddle horses, ceremonial guards and utensils were granted, and their followers also received caps and belts in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: They received seals, patents, robes, guards, and gifts; followers were rewarded in proportion.

sentences.zh: 居二十七日，三王辭歸。

translations.literal: After twenty-seven days the three kings took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-seven days the three kings departed.

sentences.zh: 各賜玉帶一，黃金百，白金二千，羅錦文綺二百，帛三百，鈔萬錠，錢二千緡，金繡蟒龍、麒麟衣各一。

translations.literal: Each was granted one jade belt, one hundred taels of gold, two thousand of white gold, two hundred bolts of brocade and patterned silk, three hundred of plain silk, ten thousand ingots of paper money, two thousand strings of cash, and one each of gold-embroidered python-dragon and qilin robes.
translations.idiomatic: Each received jade belt, gold, silver, silks, paper money, cash, and python and qilin robes.

sentences.zh: 東王次德州，卒於館。

translations.literal: The Eastern King stopped at Dezhou and died in the hostel.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern King died at Dezhou in the envoy hostel.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官賜祭，命有司營葬，勒碑墓道，謚曰恭定，留妻妾傔從十人守墓，俟畢三年喪遣歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent officials to offer sacrifice and ordered the relevant offices to prepare burial and carve a stele on the spirit way, posthumously titled Gongding; ten wives, concubines, and attendants were left to guard the tomb until the three-year mourning was complete and then sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered sacrifice, burial, a spirit stele, posthumous title Gongding, and ten attendants to guard the tomb for three years.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使齎敕諭其長子都馬含曰：「爾父知尊中國，躬率家屬陪臣，遠涉海道，萬里來朝。

translations.literal: Envoys were then sent bearing an edict to his eldest son Tumaham saying: "Your father knew how to honor China and personally led his family and attending ministers across the sea for ten thousand li to court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to his son Tumaham said: "Your father honored China and led family and ministers across the sea to court.

sentences.zh: 朕眷其誠悃，已錫王封，優加賜賚，遣官護歸。

translations.literal: I cherished his sincere devotion, already granted him royal enfeoffment, and richly bestowed gifts, sending officials to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: I enfeoffed and richly rewarded him and sent escorts home.

sentences.zh: 舟次德州，遭疾殞歿。

translations.literal: When the boat reached Dezhou he fell ill and died on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: At Dezhou he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 朕聞之，深為哀悼，已葬祭如禮。

translations.literal: When I heard this I deeply mourned him and have buried and sacrificed according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: I mourned him and buried him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 爾以嫡長，為國人所屬，宜即繼承，用綏籓服。

translations.literal: You, as the eldest legitimate son, are whom the people of the country look to; you should at once succeed to rule and settle the border state.
translations.idiomatic: As eldest son you should succeed and pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 今特封爾為蘇祿國東王。

translations.literal: Now we specially enfeoff you as Eastern King of Sulu.
translations.idiomatic: We now enfeoff you as Eastern King of Sulu.

sentences.zh: 爾尚益篤忠貞，敬承天道，以副眷懷，以繼爾父之志。

translations.literal: You should still more deepen loyal sincerity, respectfully follow Heaven's way, to fulfill Our cherishing intent and continue your father's will.
translations.idiomatic: Be ever more loyal, follow Heaven's way, and continue your father's purpose.

sentences.zh: 欽哉。」

translations.literal: Take heed!"
translations.idiomatic: Take heed!"

sentences.zh: 十八年，西王遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Western King sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 the Western King sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十九年，東王母遣王叔叭都加蘇里來朝，貢大珠一，其重七兩有奇。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Eastern King's mother sent the king's uncle Paduka Suri to court with tribute of one great pearl weighing more than seven taels.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 the Eastern Queen Mother sent the king's uncle Paduka Suri with a pearl of over seven taels.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，東王妃還國，厚賜遣之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Eastern King's consort returned home and was richly rewarded and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 the Eastern Queen returned home with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 明年入貢，自後不復至。

translations.literal: The next year they sent tribute, and thereafter they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute once more the next year, then ceased.

sentences.zh: 萬曆時，佛郎機屢攻之，城據山險，迄不能下。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period the Portuguese repeatedly attacked them; the city lay in mountainous defiles and they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli the Portuguese attacked repeatedly but could not take their mountain stronghold.

sentences.zh: 其國，於古無所考。

translations.literal: Its country cannot be verified in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Its ancient history cannot be verified.

sentences.zh: 地瘠寡粟麥，民率食魚蝦，煮海為鹽，釀蔗為酒，織竹為布。

translations.literal: The land is poor and grain and wheat scarce; the people mostly eat fish and shrimp, boil the sea for salt, ferment sugarcane for wine, and weave bamboo for cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Soil is thin and grain scarce; people live on fish and shrimp, sea salt, sugar wine, and bamboo cloth.

sentences.zh: 氣候常熱。

translations.literal: The climate is constantly hot.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is perpetually hot.

sentences.zh: 有珠池，夜望之，光浮水面。

translations.literal: There is a pearl bed; at night one looks and light floats on the water's surface.
translations.idiomatic: There is a pearl fishery whose beds glow on the water at night.

sentences.zh: 土人以珠與華人市易，大者利數十倍。

translations.literal: The natives trade pearls with Chinese, and large ones yield profits several tens of times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Natives trade pearls with Chinese; large ones bring tenfold profit.

sentences.zh: 商舶將返，輒留數人為質，冀其再來。

translations.literal: When merchant ships were about to return, they would leave several men as hostages, hoping they would come again.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant ships often left hostages behind, hoping for return voyages.

sentences.zh: 其旁近國名高藥，出玳瑁。

translations.literal: A neighboring state called Gaoyao produces tortoiseshell.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby Gaoyao produces tortoiseshell.

sentences.zh: 西洋瑣裡

translations.literal: Western Chola
translations.idiomatic: Western Chola

sentences.zh: 西洋瑣裡，洪武二年命使臣劉叔勉以即位詔諭其國。

translations.literal: Western Chola: in the second year of Hongwu the envoy Liu Shumian was ordered to announce the accession edict to the country.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 2 Liu Shumian was sent with the accession edict to Western Chola.

sentences.zh: 三年平定沙漠，復遣使臣頒詔。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the desert was pacified, envoys were again sent to proclaim the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, after the desert campaign, envoys proclaimed the edict again.

sentences.zh: 其王別裡提遣使奉金葉表，從叔勉獻方物。

translations.literal: Its king Beritte sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial, following Shumian to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: King Beritte sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial and goods with Shumian.

sentences.zh: 賜文綺、紗羅諸物甚厚，並賜《大統歷》。

translations.literal: They were granted patterned silks, gauze, and silk in great abundance, and also the Comprehensive Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted rich silks and the Comprehensive Calendar.

sentences.zh: 成祖頒即位詔於海外諸國，西洋亦與焉。

translations.literal: When Chengzu proclaimed the accession edict to overseas states, the Western Ocean was also included.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu's accession edict reached the Western Ocean states as well.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年命副使聞良輔、行人甯善使其國，賜絨錦、文綺、紗羅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle Deputy Envoy Wen Liangfu and Courier Ning Shan were sent to the country, granting pile velvet, patterned silk, and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 1 Wen Liangfu and Ning Shan were sent with velvets and silks.

sentences.zh: 已，覆命中官馬彬往使，賜如前。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the eunuch Ma Bin was again ordered to go as envoy, with gifts as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon eunuch Ma Bin was sent with the same gifts.

sentences.zh: 其王即遣使來貢，附載胡椒與民市。

translations.literal: Its king at once sent envoys with tribute, bringing pepper to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent envoys with pepper for trade.

sentences.zh: 有司請徵稅，命勿徵。

translations.literal: The relevant offices asked to levy taxes; the Emperor ordered that none be levied.
translations.idiomatic: Offices asked to tax the trade; the emperor forbade it.

sentences.zh: 二十一年偕古裡、阿丹等十五國來貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year it came with Calicut, Aden, and fifteen other states to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 it joined Calicut, Aden, and fifteen states in tribute.

sentences.zh: 瑣裡，近西洋瑣裡而差小。

translations.literal: Chola lies near Western Chola but is somewhat smaller.
translations.idiomatic: Chola lies near Western Chola but is smaller.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，命使臣塔海帖木兒齎詔撫諭其國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu the envoy Taqai Temur was ordered to carry an edict to comfort and instruct the country.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 Taqai Temur carried an edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 五年，王卜納的遣使奉表朝貢，並獻其國土地山川圖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year King Punakad sent envoys with a memorial and court tribute, also presenting a map of the country's land, mountains, and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 King Punakad sent tribute and a map of the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝顧中書省臣曰：「西洋諸國素稱遠蕃，涉海而來，難計歲月。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to members of the Secretariat: "The states of the Western Ocean have long been called distant barbarians; crossing the sea to come, one cannot count the months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: "Western Ocean states are far across the sea; voyages take uncounted months.

sentences.zh: 其朝貢無論疏數，厚往薄來可也。」

translations.literal: Whether tribute missions are frequent or rare, generous giving and light receiving will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Whether they come often or seldom, give generously and receive lightly.

sentences.zh: 乃賜《大統歷》及金織文綺、紗羅各四匹，使者亦賜幣帛有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were granted the Comprehensive Calendar and four bolts each of gold-woven brocade, gauze, and silk; the envoys also received silks in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: They received the calendar, silks, and envoys gifts in proportion.

sentences.zh: 覽邦，在西南海中。

translations.literal: Kampar lies in the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Kampar lies in the southwestern ocean.

sentences.zh: 洪武九年，王昔裡馬哈剌札的剌札遣使奉表來貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongwu King Siri Maharaja Zainal sent envoys with a memorial and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 9 King Siri Maharaja Zainal sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔賜其王織金文綺、紗羅，使者宴賜如制。

translations.literal: An edict granted the king gold-woven brocades and gauze, and the envoys were feasted and rewarded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The king received brocades and envoys were feasted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 永樂、宣德中，嘗附鄰國朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Yongle and Xuande periods they sometimes joined neighboring states in tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle and Xuande they sometimes joined neighbors in tribute.

sentences.zh: 其地多沙礫，麻麥之外無他種。

translations.literal: The land has much gravel; apart from hemp and grain there are no other crops.
translations.idiomatic: The soil is gravelly; only hemp and grain grow.

sentences.zh: 商賈鮮至。

translations.literal: Merchants rarely came.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants seldom came.

sentences.zh: 山坦迤無峰巒，水亦淺濁。

translations.literal: The mountains spread level without peaks and ridges; the water is also shallow and turbid.
translations.idiomatic: Hills are low and waters shallow and muddy.

sentences.zh: 俗好佛，勤賽祀。

translations.literal: The people love the Buddha and diligently perform sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: People are devout Buddhists and diligent in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 厥貢，孔雀、馬、檀香、降香、胡椒、蘇木。

translations.literal: Their tribute included peacocks, horses, sandalwood, eaglewood, pepper, and sappanwood.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included peacocks, horses, sandalwood, eaglewood, pepper, and sappanwood.

sentences.zh: 交易用錢。

translations.literal: Trade used money.
translations.idiomatic: They traded with coin.

sentences.zh: 淡巴，亦西南海中國。

translations.literal: Lampung is also a state in the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Lampung is another state in the southwestern sea.

sentences.zh: 洪武十年，其王佛喝思羅遣使上表，貢方物，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Hongwu its king Fakhr al-Din sent envoys with a memorial and local products; gifts were granted in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 10 King Fakhr al-Din sent tribute and received gifts in proportion.

sentences.zh: 其國，石城瓦屋。

translations.literal: In the country are stone walls and tiled roofs.
translations.idiomatic: Its towns have stone walls and tiled roofs.

sentences.zh: 王乘輿，官跨馬，有中國威儀。

translations.literal: The king rides in a carriage; officials ride horses; there is Chinese ceremonial dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The king uses a carriage, officials ride horses, and ceremony resembles China's.

sentences.zh: 土衍水清，草木暢茂，畜產甚伙。

translations.literal: The soil extends and the water is clear; plants and trees flourish luxuriantly, and livestock are very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Land is fertile, water clear, vegetation lush, and livestock abundant.

sentences.zh: 男女勤於耕織，市有貿易，野無寇盜，稱樂土焉。

translations.literal: Men and women are diligent in farming and weaving; there is trade in the markets, no bandits in the wilds—it is called a happy land.
translations.idiomatic: People farm and weave diligently; markets thrive and the land is peaceful.

sentences.zh: 厥貢，苾布、兜羅綿被、沉香、速香、檀香、胡椒。

translations.literal: Their tribute included cotton cloth, tulle cotton quilts, aloeswood, gharuwood, sandalwood, and pepper.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included cottons, quilts, aloeswood, gharuwood, sandalwood, and pepper.

sentences.zh: 百花，居西南海中。

translations.literal: Baihua lies in the southwestern sea.
translations.idiomatic: Baihua lies in the southwestern sea.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年，其王剌丁剌者望沙遣使奉金葉表，貢白鹿、紅猴、龜筒、玳瑁、孔雀、鸚鵡、哇哇倒掛鳥及胡椒、香、蠟諸物。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu its king Raden Zainal sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial, presenting a white deer, red monkey, tortoiseshell tubes, tortoiseshell, peacocks, parrots, hanging parrots, and pepper, incense, wax, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 11 King Raden Zainal sent a white deer, rare animals, aromatics, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 詔賜王及使者綺、幣、襲衣有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted the king and envoys brocades, silks, and investiture robes in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: King and envoys received silks and robes in proportion.

sentences.zh: 國中氣候恆燠，無霜雪，多奇花異卉，故名百花。

translations.literal: In the country the climate is always warm; there is no frost or snow, and many strange flowers and exotic plants—hence the name Baihua.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is always warm, without frost; rare flowers abound—hence the name Baihua, "Hundred Flowers."

sentences.zh: 民富饒，尚釋教。

translations.literal: The people are rich and revere Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: The people are wealthy and Buddhist.

sentences.zh: 彭亨

translations.literal: Pahang
translations.idiomatic: Pahang

sentences.zh: （Pahang，馬來半島最大的州）〉

translations.literal: (Pahang, the largest state on the Malay Peninsula)〉 (closing editorial note)〉
translations.idiomatic: Pahang, the largest state on the Malay Peninsula)〉

sentences.zh: 彭亨，在暹羅之西。

translations.literal: Pahang lies west of Siam.
translations.idiomatic: Pahang lies west of Siam.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年，其王麻哈剌惹答饒遣使齎金葉表，貢番奴六人及方物，宴賚如禮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu its king Maharaja Dewa sent envoys with a gold-leaf memorial, presenting six barbarian slaves and local products; they were feasted and rewarded according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 11 King Maharaja Dewa sent six slaves and goods and was feasted by ritual.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年，王巴剌密瑣剌達羅息泥遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle King Paduka Maulana sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 9 King Paduka Maulana sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十年，鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zheng He was sent to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Zheng He visited.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復入貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they again sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十四年，與古裡、爪哇諸國偕貢，復令鄭和報之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year they joined Calicut, Java, and other states in tribute, and Zheng He was again ordered to return the visit.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 they joined Calicut and Java in tribute and Zheng He returned the visit.

sentences.zh: 其國，土田沃，氣候常溫，米粟饒足，煮海為鹽，釀椰漿為酒。

translations.literal: In the country the fields are fertile, the climate always mild, rice and grain abundant; they boil the sea for salt and ferment coconut sap for wine.
translations.idiomatic: Fields are fertile, climate mild, grain plentiful; they make salt from the sea and wine from coconuts.

sentences.zh: 上下親狎，無寇賊。

translations.literal: Superiors and inferiors are intimate; there are no bandits.
translations.idiomatic: People live in harmony without banditry.

sentences.zh: 然惑於鬼神，刻香木為像，殺人祭賽，以禳災祈福。

translations.literal: Yet they are deluded by ghosts and spirits; they carve spirit images from fragrant wood, kill people in sacrifice, and seek to avert disaster and pray for blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they worship spirits, carve incense-wood images, and sacrifice human lives for blessings.

sentences.zh: 所貢有像牙、片腦、乳香、速香、檀香、胡椒、蘇木之屬。

translations.literal: Tribute included ivory, camphor flakes, olibanum, gharuwood, sandalwood, pepper, and sappanwood.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute included ivory, camphor, frankincense, gharuwood, sandalwood, pepper, and sappanwood.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆時，有柔佛國副王子娶彭亨王女，將婚，副王送子至彭亨，彭亨王置酒，親戚畢會。

translations.literal: By the Wanli period the vice-prince of Johor married the daughter of the king of Pahang; when the marriage was to take place the vice-prince sent his son to Pahang, and the king of Pahang set out wine with all kin assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli Johor's vice-prince wed Pahang's princess; the bridegroom was sent to Pahang for the wedding feast with all kin present.

sentences.zh: 婆羅國王子為彭亨王妹婿，舉觴獻副王，而手指有巨珠甚美，副王欲之，許以重賄。

translations.literal: The prince of Brunei was son-in-law to the king of Pahang's sister; raising his cup to toast the vice-prince, he had a huge and beautiful pearl on his finger; the vice-prince desired it and promised heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Brunei's prince, Pahang's sister's husband, wore a great pearl at the toast; the vice-prince coveted it and offered bribes.

sentences.zh: 王子靳不予，副王怒，即歸國發兵來攻。

translations.literal: The prince was reluctant to give it; the vice-prince was angry and at once returned home to raise troops and attack.
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused; the vice-prince returned home and raised an army.

sentences.zh: 彭亨人出不意，不戰自潰。

translations.literal: The people of Pahang, caught unawares, did not fight and scattered of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Pahang was taken unawares and collapsed without a fight.

sentences.zh: 王與婆羅王子奔金山。

translations.literal: The king and the prince of Brunei fled to Golden Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The king and Brunei's prince fled to Golden Mountain.

sentences.zh: 浡泥國王，王妃兄也，聞之，率眾來援。

translations.literal: The king of Brunei, brother to the queen consort, heard of this and led troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Brunei's king, the queen's brother, marched to their aid.

sentences.zh: 副王乃大肆焚掠而去。

translations.literal: The vice-prince then plundered and burned on a great scale and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The vice-prince looted and burned widely, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 當是時，國中鬼哭三日，人民半死。

translations.literal: At that time in the country ghosts wailed for three days and half the people died.
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts were said to wail for three days and half the people perished.

sentences.zh: 浡泥王迎其妹歸，彭亨王隨之，而命其長子攝國。

translations.literal: The king of Brunei welcomed his sister home; the king of Pahang followed, leaving his eldest son to govern the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Brunei's king escorted his sister home; Pahang's king followed, leaving his eldest son as regent.

sentences.zh: 已，王復位，次子素凶悍，遂毒殺其父，弒其兄自立。

translations.literal: Later the king resumed the throne; his second son was by nature fierce and cruel, and he therefore poisoned his father, murdered his elder brother, and usurped rule himself.
translations.idiomatic: The king returned, but his fierce second son poisoned him, slew his brother, and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 那孤兒

translations.literal: Nakur
translations.idiomatic: Nakur

sentences.zh: （Nanggroë，今之亞齊，位於印度尼西亞蘇門答臘島北端。）〉

translations.literal: (Nanggroë, present-day Aceh, at the northern tip of Sumatra in Indonesia)〉 (closing editorial note)〉
translations.idiomatic: Nanggroë, present-day Aceh, at the northern tip of Sumatra in Indonesia)〉

sentences.zh: 那孤兒，以蘇門答剌之西，壤相接。

translations.literal: Nakur borders Sumatra to the west with contiguous territory.
translations.idiomatic: Nakur lies west of Sumatra on contiguous ground.

sentences.zh: 地狹，止千餘家。

translations.literal: The land is narrow, with only a little more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The territory is small, barely a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 男子皆以墨剌面為花獸之狀，故又名花面國。

translations.literal: Men all tattoo their faces with designs of flowers and beasts in ink, hence it is also called the Flower-Face Country.
translations.idiomatic: Men tattoo their faces with floral and animal designs—hence the Flower-Face Country.

sentences.zh: 猱頭裸體，男女止單布圍腰。

translations.literal: They have monkey-like heads and naked bodies; men and women wear only a single cloth about the waist.
translations.idiomatic: They go bare except for a waist cloth.

sentences.zh: 然俗淳，田足稻禾，強不侵弱，富不驕貧，悉自耕而食，無寇盜。

translations.literal: Yet customs are honest; fields suffice for rice; the strong do not invade the weak, the rich do not despise the poor; all eat what they themselves cultivate, and there are no bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Customs are honest, rice sufficient, the strong do not prey on the weak, and there is no banditry.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period Zheng He was sent to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle Zheng He visited.

sentences.zh: 其酋長常入貢方物。

translations.literal: Its chieftains often entered with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Its chiefs often sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 黎伐，在那孤兒之西。

translations.literal: Lide lies west of Nakur.
translations.idiomatic: Lide lies west of Nakur.

sentences.zh: 南大山，北大海，西接南渤利。

translations.literal: Mountains to the south, great sea to the north, bordering Lamuri to the west.
translations.idiomatic: It has mountains to the south, sea to the north, and borders Lamuri on the west.

sentences.zh: 居民三千家，推一人為主。

translations.literal: Residents number three thousand households, choosing one man as chief.
translations.idiomatic: About three thousand households choose one chief.

sentences.zh: 隸蘇門答剌，聲音風俗多與之同。

translations.literal: Subject to Sumatra, their speech and customs largely resemble its.
translations.idiomatic: It is subject to Sumatra and shares its speech and customs.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，嘗隨其使臣入貢。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period they sometimes followed its envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle they sometimes joined Sumatra's envoys in tribute.

sentences.zh: 南渤利

translations.literal: Lamuri
translations.idiomatic: Lamuri

sentences.zh: 南渤利，在蘇門答剌之西。

translations.literal: Lamuri lies west of Sumatra.
translations.idiomatic: Lamuri lies west of Sumatra.

sentences.zh: 順風三日夜可至。

translations.literal: With a fair wind one can reach it in three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: With fair winds it is three days and nights' sail.

sentences.zh: 王及居民皆回回人，僅千餘家。

translations.literal: The king and inhabitants are all Muslims, barely more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: King and people are Muslim, barely a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 俗樸實，地少谷，人多食魚蝦。

translations.literal: Customs are simple and honest; grain is scarce on land and people mostly eat fish and shrimp.
translations.idiomatic: Customs are plain; grain is scarce and people live on fish and shrimp.

sentences.zh: 西北海中有山甚高大，曰帽山，其西復大海，名那沒黎洋，西來洋船俱望此山為準。

translations.literal: In the northwestern sea there is a very tall mountain called Hat Mountain; west of it is again a great sea called the Namuli Ocean, and ships from the Western Ocean all take this mountain as their bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest stands Hat Mountain; beyond it lies the Namuli Ocean, the bearing for Western Ocean ships.

sentences.zh: 近山淺水內，生珊瑚樹，高者三尺許。

translations.literal: In shallow water near the mountain coral trees grow, the tall ones about three feet.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow waters near the mountain grow coral trees up to three feet.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年，其王馬哈麻沙遣使附蘇門答剌使入貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle its king Mahmud Shah sent envoys attached to Sumatra's mission with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 10 King Mahmud Shah sent envoys with Sumatra's tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜其使襲衣，賜王印誥、錦綺、羅紗、彩幣。

translations.literal: Investiture robes were granted to the envoys, and the king was granted seal, patent, brocades, gauze, silk, and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys received robes; the king received seal, patent, and silks.

sentences.zh: 遣鄭和撫諭其國。

translations.literal: Zheng He was sent to comfort and instruct the country.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He was sent to reassure the realm.

sentences.zh: 終成祖時，比年入貢，其王子沙者罕亦遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Throughout Chengzu's reign tribute came yearly, and the prince Shah Jahan also sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Through Chengzu's reign tribute came yearly; Prince Shah Jahan also sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，鄭和遍賜諸國，南渤利亦與焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande Zheng He bestowed gifts on all the states, and Lamuri was also included.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 Zheng He's gifts reached Lamuri as well.

sentences.zh: 阿魯，一名啞魯，近滿剌加。

translations.literal: Aru, also called Ya-lu, lies near Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: Aru, also called Yalu, lies near Malacca.

sentences.zh: 順風三日夜可達。

translations.literal: With a fair wind one can reach it in three days and nights.
translations.idiomatic: With fair winds it is three days and nights' sail.

sentences.zh: 風俗、氣候大類蘇門答剌。

translations.literal: Customs and climate largely resemble Sumatra's.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and climate resemble Sumatra's.

sentences.zh: 田瘠少收，盛藝芭蕉、椰子為食。

translations.literal: Fields are poor and harvests small; they plant bananas and coconuts in abundance for food.
translations.idiomatic: Fields are thin; they live mainly on bananas and coconuts.

sentences.zh: 男女皆裸體，以布圍腰。

translations.literal: Men and women are all naked, wearing only cloth about the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women go bare except for waist cloths.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年，王速魯唐忽先遣使附古裡諸國入貢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle King Sultan Ahmad sent envoys attached to Calicut and other states with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 9 King Sultan Ahmad sent envoys with Calicut's tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜其使冠帶、彩幣、寶鈔，其王亦有賜。

translations.literal: His envoys were granted caps, belts, colored silks, and treasure notes, and the king also received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys received caps, silks, and paper money; the king was rewarded as well.

sentences.zh: 十年，鄭和使其國。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zheng He was sent to their country.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Zheng He visited.

sentences.zh: 十七年，王子段阿剌沙遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the prince Tuan Alaksa sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 Prince Tuan Alaksa sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十九年、二十一年，再入貢。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth and twenty-first years they again sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In years 19 and 21 they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，鄭和使諸蕃，亦有賜。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande, when Zheng He was sent to the various barbarian states, gifts were also bestowed there.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 5 Zheng He's mission brought gifts there too.

sentences.zh: 其後貢使不至。

translations.literal: After that tribute envoys did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter no tribute envoys came.

sentences.zh: 柔佛，近彭亨，一名烏丁礁林。

translations.literal: Johor lies near Pahang and is also called Wuding Jiaolin.
translations.idiomatic: Johor, near Pahang, is also called Wuding Jiaolin.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，鄭和遍歷西洋，無柔佛名。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period Zheng He traversed the Western Ocean, and there was no state called Johor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle Zheng He's voyages listed no state called Johor.

sentences.zh: 或言和曾經東西竺山，今此山正在其地，疑即東西竺。

translations.literal: Some say He once passed East and West Zhu Mountain, which now stands in that region—perhaps it is East-West Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Some say he passed East-West Zhu Mountain, now in that region.

sentences.zh: 萬曆間，其酋好構兵，鄰國丁機宜、彭亨屢被其患。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period its chieftain loved raising troops; neighboring Terengganu and Pahang were repeatedly troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli its chief warred often; Terengganu and Pahang suffered repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 華人販他國者多就之貿易，時或邀至其國。

translations.literal: Chinese who traded in other countries often traded with him, and he sometimes invited them to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese merchants trading abroad often dealt with him and were sometimes invited to his realm.

sentences.zh: 國中覆茅為屋，列木為城，環以池。

translations.literal: In the country they thatch roofs for houses, set timbers for walls, and surround them with moats.
translations.idiomatic: Houses are thatched, palisades set as walls, and moats dug around.

sentences.zh: 無事通商於外，有事則召募為兵，稱強國焉。

translations.literal: When at peace they trade abroad; when there is trouble they recruit soldiers and are called a strong state.
translations.idiomatic: In peace they trade abroad; in war they recruit troops and are reckoned strong.

sentences.zh: 地不產谷，常易米於鄰壤。

translations.literal: The land produces no grain and regularly barters rice from neighboring regions.
translations.idiomatic: No grain grows; they trade for rice from neighbors.

sentences.zh: 男子薙發徒跣佩刀，女子蓄髮椎結，其酋則佩雙刀。

translations.literal: Men shave their heads, go barefoot, and wear swords; women keep their hair and wear it in topknots; the chieftain wears two swords.
translations.idiomatic: Men are shaven, barefoot, and armed; women wear topknots; the chief wears twin swords.

sentences.zh: 字用茭曌葉，以刀刺之。

translations.literal: Writing uses palm leaves, incised with knives.
translations.idiomatic: They write on palm leaves cut with knives.

sentences.zh: 婚姻亦論門閥。

translations.literal: Marriage also considers family standing.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage observes rank and lineage.

sentences.zh: 王用金銀為食器，群下則用磁。

translations.literal: The king uses gold and silver for eating vessels; his subordinates use porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: The king eats from gold and silver; subjects use porcelain.

sentences.zh: 無匕箸。

translations.literal: There are no spoons or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: They use neither spoons nor chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 俗好持齋，見星方食。

translations.literal: Custom favors fasting; they eat only when stars appear.
translations.idiomatic: They fast by custom and eat only after nightfall.

sentences.zh: 節序以四月為歲首。

translations.literal: The seasons take the fourth month as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Their year begins in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 居喪，婦人薙發，男子則重薙，死者皆火葬。

translations.literal: In mourning women shave their heads and men shave again more heavily; the dead are all cremated.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning women shave their heads; men shave again; the dead are cremated.

sentences.zh: 所產有犀、象、玳瑁、片腦、沒藥、血竭、錫、蠟、嘉文簟、木棉花、檳榔、海菜、窩燕、西國米、跂吉柿之屬。

translations.literal: Products include rhinoceros, elephants, tortoiseshell, camphor flakes, myrrh, dragon's blood, tin, wax, fine woven mats, kapok, betel, seaweed, edible-nest swiftlets, Western rice, and persimmons.
translations.idiomatic: They produce rhinoceros, ivory, tortoiseshell, camphor, myrrh, dragon's blood, tin, wax, fine mats, kapok, betel, bird's nests, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 始其國吉寧仁為大庫，忠於王，為王所倚信。

translations.literal: Originally in the country Jining Ren was grand treasurer, loyal to the king and relied on and trusted by him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jining Ren was grand treasurer, loyal and trusted by the king.

sentences.zh: 王弟以兄疏己，潛殺之。

translations.literal: The king's younger brother, because his elder kept him at a distance, secretly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The king's brother, feeling slighted, secretly killed him.

sentences.zh: 後出行墮馬死，左右咸見吉寧仁為祟，自是家家祀之。

translations.literal: Later, going out, the king fell from his horse and died; those about him all saw Jining Ren as a haunting spirit, and from then on every household sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: The king later fell from his horse and died; all saw Jining Ren's ghost, and every household thereafter worshipped him.

sentences.zh: 丁機宜

translations.literal: Terengganu
translations.idiomatic: Terengganu

sentences.zh: 丁機宜，爪哇屬國也，幅員甚狹，僅千餘家。

translations.literal: Terengganu was a subject state of Java, very narrow in extent, barely more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Terengganu, a Javanese dependency, was tiny—barely a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 柔佛黠而雄，丁機宜與接壤，時被其患。

translations.literal: Johor was cunning and powerful; Terengganu bordered it and was often troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Johor was fierce; Terengganu, adjoining it, suffered often.

sentences.zh: 後以厚幣求婚，稍獲寧處。

translations.literal: Later, by heavy bride-price in marriage, it obtained a little peace.
translations.idiomatic: Later a marriage alliance bought a little peace.

sentences.zh: 其國以木為城。

translations.literal: The country used timber for its walls.
translations.idiomatic: Its walls were of timber.

sentences.zh: 酋所居，旁列鐘鼓樓，出入乘象。

translations.literal: Where the chieftain dwelt, bell and drum towers stood at the side; going out and in he rode an elephant.
translations.idiomatic: The chief's residence had bell and drum towers; he rode an elephant abroad.

sentences.zh: 以十月為歲首。

translations.literal: The tenth month was taken as the year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Their year began in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 性好潔，酋所食啖，皆躬自割烹。

translations.literal: They loved cleanliness; what the chieftain ate and drank he always cut and cooked himself.
translations.idiomatic: The chief was fastidious and cooked his own food.

sentences.zh: 民俗類爪哇，物產悉如柔佛。

translations.literal: Folk customs resembled Java's; products were all like Johor's.
translations.idiomatic: Customs resembled Java's; products matched Johor's.

sentences.zh: 酒禁甚嚴，有常稅。

translations.literal: The ban on wine was very strict, with a regular tax.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was strictly forbidden and taxed.

sentences.zh: 然大家皆不飲，維細民無籍者飲之，其曹偶咸非笑。

translations.literal: Yet great families all abstained; only common people without registers drank, and their companions did not mock them.
translations.idiomatic: Great families did not drink; only unregistered commoners did, without reproach.

sentences.zh: 婚者，男往女家持其門戶，故生女勝男。

translations.literal: In marriage the man went to the woman's house and held her household, so bearing daughters was preferred to sons.
translations.idiomatic: The groom joined the wife's household, so daughters were prized over sons.

sentences.zh: 喪用火葬。

translations.literal: The dead were cremated.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated.

sentences.zh: 華人往商，交易甚平。

translations.literal: Chinese who went to trade found dealings very fair.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese traders found the market fair.

sentences.zh: 自為柔佛所破，往者亦鮮。

translations.literal: Since being broken by Johor, few went there.
translations.idiomatic: After Johor's conquest few traders went.

sentences.zh: 巴剌西

translations.literal: Safavid Persia
translations.idiomatic: Safavid Persia

sentences.zh: 巴剌西，去中國絕遠。

translations.literal: Safavid Persia is extremely far from China.
translations.idiomatic: Safavid Persia lies immensely far from China.

sentences.zh: 正德六年遣使臣沙地白入貢，言其國在南海，始奉王命來朝，舟行四年半，遭風飄至西瀾海，舟壞，止存一小艇，又飄流八日，至得吉零國，居一年。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde its envoy Shadi Bai entered with tribute, saying its country was in the southern sea; obeying the king's command it came to court for the first time; the boat had sailed four and a half years, met wind and was driven to the Western Ocean, the boat was wrecked and only a small skiff remained; after drifting eight more days they reached the country of Dejiling and lived there one year.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 6 envoy Shadi Bai said their first mission had sailed four and a half years, been wrecked, drifted to Dejiling for a year.

sentences.zh: 至秘得，居八月。

translations.literal: They reached Bimi and lived there eight months.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Bimi and stayed eight months.

sentences.zh: 乃遵陸行，閱二十六日抵暹羅，以情告王，獲賜日給，且賜婦女四人，居四年。

translations.literal: Then they traveled by land; after twenty-six days they reached Siam, told the king their story, received daily provisions, and were also given four women; they lived there four years.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty-six days overland they reached Siam, were fed, given four wives, and stayed four years.

sentences.zh: 迄今年五月始附番舶入廣東，得達闕下。

translations.literal: Only in the fifth month of this year did they attach to a barbarian ship and enter Guangdong, reaching the court below.
translations.idiomatic: This fifth month they reached Guangdong on a foreign ship and came to court.

sentences.zh: 進金葉表，貢祖母綠一，珊瑚樹、琉璃瓶、玻璃盞各四，及瑪瑙珠、胡黑丹諸物。

translations.literal: They presented a gold-leaf memorial and tribute of one emerald, four each of coral trees, glass bottles, and glass cups, and agate beads, foreign black cinnabar, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: They presented a gold memorial, an emerald, coral, glassware, agate, cinnabar, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其遠來，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended their coming from afar and granted rewards with additions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised their distant journey and rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 佛郎機

translations.literal: Portugal
translations.idiomatic: Portugal

sentences.zh: 佛郎機，近滿剌加。

translations.literal: Portugal lies near Malacca.
translations.idiomatic: Portugal lies near Malacca.

sentences.zh: 正德中，據滿剌加地，逐其王。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period it seized Malacca's territory and drove out its king.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde it seized Malacca and expelled its king.

sentences.zh: 十三年遣使臣加必丹末等貢方物，請封，始知其名。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year envoys including Qabidin sent local products and asked for enfeoffment; only then was its name known.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 envoys sought enfeoffment; only then was Portugal known by name.

sentences.zh: 詔給方物之直，遣還。

translations.literal: An edict granted the value of the tribute goods and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: The court paid for their goods and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 其人久留不去，剽劫行旅，至掠小兒為食。

translations.literal: Their people long remained and would not leave, plundering travelers and even seizing small children for food.
translations.idiomatic: They stayed on, robbed travelers, and even ate small children.

sentences.zh: 已而夤緣鎮守中貴，許入京。

translations.literal: Later they curried favor with the guarding eunuchs and were permitted to enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later they bribed guarding eunuchs and entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 武宗南巡，其使火者亞三因江彬侍帝左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong toured the south, their envoy the fire-officer Yasang, through Jiang Bin, attended the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: On Wuzong's southern tour the envoy Yasang attended him through Jiang Bin.

sentences.zh: 帝時學其語以為戲。

translations.literal: The Emperor then learned their language for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor even learned their language for sport.

sentences.zh: 其留懷遠驛者，益掠買良民，築室立寨，為久居計。

translations.literal: Those who remained at the Hostel for Tributary Envoys plundered and bought good people all the more, built houses and stockades, and planned long residence.
translations.idiomatic: Those at the tributary hostel kidnapped subjects, built compounds, and planned to stay.

sentences.zh: 十五年，御史丘道隆言：「滿剌加乃敕封之國，而佛郎機敢並之，且啖我以利，邀求封貢，決不可許。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Supervising Secretary Qiu Daolong said: "Malacca is a state enfeoffed by imperial command, yet Portugal dares annex it, and moreover tempts us with profit and seeks enfeoffment and tribute—this must on no account be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 Qiu Daolong said: "Malacca is an enfeoffed ally; Portugal has seized it and seeks trade and titles—that must be refused.

sentences.zh: 宜卻其使臣，明示順逆，令還滿剌加疆土，方許朝貢。

translations.literal: Send back their envoys, make clear loyalty and rebellion, and require restoration of Malacca's territory before tribute may be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Send their envoys back, show loyalty from rebellion, and restore Malacca before any tribute.

sentences.zh: 倘執迷不悛，必檄告諸蕃，聲罪致討。」

translations.literal: If they persist in error, edicts must inform the various barbarian states and proclaim guilt to launch punitive action.
translations.idiomatic: If they persist, proclaim their crime to all maritime states and punish them.

sentences.zh: 御史何鰲言：「佛郎機最凶狡，兵械較諸蕃獨精。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary He Ao said: "Portugal is most fierce and cunning; its arms surpass all other barbarian states.
translations.idiomatic: He Ao said: "Portugal is fiercest and best armed of all maritime powers.

sentences.zh: 前歲駕大舶突入廣東會城，礮聲殷地。

translations.literal: In former years great ships suddenly entered Guangdong's provincial city; cannon thunder shook the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Last year great ships entered Guangdong; cannon shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 留驛者違制交通，入都者桀驁爭長。

translations.literal: Those who remained at the hostel violated regulations in dealings; those who entered the capital were arrogant and contentious.
translations.idiomatic: Hostel dwellers traded illegally; those in the capital were insolent.

sentences.zh: 今聽其往來貿易，勢必爭鬥殺傷，南方之禍殆無紀極。

translations.literal: If they are now allowed to come and go in trade, fighting and killing will surely follow, and calamity in the south may know no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Allow free trade and bloodshed will follow without end in the south.

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝貢有定期，防有常制，故來者不多。

translations.literal: In the ancestors' time tribute had fixed seasons and defense had regular systems, so few came.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly tribute had fixed seasons and strict defense, so few came.

sentences.zh: 近因布政吳廷舉謂缺上供香物，不問何年，來即取貨。

translations.literal: Recently because Provincial Commissioner Wu Tingju said tribute incense for the court was lacking, without asking what year, whenever they came goods were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Wu Tingju, lacking court incense, took goods whenever ships came.

sentences.zh: 致番舶不絕於海澨，蠻人雜遝於州城。

translations.literal: This caused barbarian ships never to cease on the coast and barbarian men to throng the prefectural cities.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian ships crowded the coast and foreigners packed the cities.

sentences.zh: 禁防既疏，水道益熟。

translations.literal: Defenses grew lax and sea routes familiar.
translations.idiomatic: Defenses slackened and sea lanes grew familiar.

sentences.zh: 此佛郎機所以乘機突至也。

translations.literal: This is how Portugal seized the chance to burst in.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Portugal burst in.

sentences.zh: 乞悉驅在澳番舶及番人潛居者，禁私通，嚴守備，庶一方獲安。」

translations.literal: I beg that all Portuguese ships at Macao and Portuguese living in hiding be driven off, private trade forbidden, and defenses strictly kept—then one region may be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Drive out Portuguese ships and residents, forbid private trade, and strengthen defenses."

sentences.zh: 疏下禮部，言：「道隆先宰順德，鰲即順德人，故深晰利害。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of Rites, which said: "Daolong formerly governed Shunde, and Ao is a man of Shunde, so they deeply understand the harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites noted both memorialists knew the coast well.

sentences.zh: 宜俟滿剌加使臣至，廷詰佛郎機侵奪鄰邦、擾亂內地之罪，奏請處置。

translations.literal: When Malacca's envoys arrive, question Portugal in court about seizing a neighboring state and disturbing the inner lands, memorialize and request disposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Malacca's envoys come, try Portugal for seizing neighbors and disorder inland.

sentences.zh: 其他悉如御史言。」

translations.literal: All else should follow the censors' words."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise follow the censors' advice.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted."
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 亞三侍帝驕甚。

translations.literal: Yasang attended the Emperor and was very arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Yasang grew insolent in the emperor's company.

sentences.zh: 從駕入都，居會同館。

translations.literal: Following the imperial tour into the capital, he lodged at the Hostel for Tributary Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital with the tour and lodged at the tributary hostel.

sentences.zh: 見提督主事梁焯，不屈膝。

translations.literal: Seeing Chief Director Liang Chao, he would not kneel.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to kneel to Chief Director Liang Chao.

sentences.zh: 焯怒，撻之。

translations.literal: Chao was angry and had him flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Chao had him beaten in anger.

sentences.zh: 彬大詬曰：「彼嘗與天子嬉戲，肯跪汝小官邪？」

translations.literal: Bin loudly reviled him, saying: "He once played with the Son of Heaven—would he kneel to a petty officer like you?
translations.idiomatic: Bin shouted: "He played with the emperor—why kneel to you?

sentences.zh: 明年，武宗崩，亞三下吏。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Wuzong died and Yasang was handed to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Wuzong died and Yasang was arrested.

sentences.zh: 自言本華人，為番人所使，乃伏法，絕其朝貢。

translations.literal: He himself said he was originally Chinese, employed by the barbarians, and then submitted to the law; tribute was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed he was Chinese in barbarian employ and was executed; tribute ceased.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，又以接濟朝使為詞，攜土物求市。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year they again, on the pretext of supplying the tribute mission, brought local goods seeking trade.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month they sought trade again, claiming to supply the tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 守臣請抽分如故事，詔復拒之。

translations.literal: The guarding officials asked to levy shares as of old; an edict again refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials asked to tax trade as before; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 其將別都盧既以巨礮利兵肆掠滿剌加諸國，橫行海上，復率其屬疏世利等駕五舟，擊破巴西國。

translations.literal: Their general Betudo, with great cannon and sharp arms, had plundered Malacca and other states and ranged the sea; he again led his followers Shilishi and others in five ships and smashed the state of Brazil.
translations.idiomatic: General Betudo, with great guns, had raided Malacca and the seas and smashed Brazil with five ships.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年遂寇新會之西草灣，指揮柯榮、百戶王應恩御之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing they then raided Xicao Bay in Xinhui; Commander Ke Rong and Company Commander Wang Ying'en resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 2 they raided Xinhui's Xicao Bay; Ke Rong and Wang Ying'en resisted.

sentences.zh: 轉戰至稍州，向化人潘丁苟先登，眾齊進，生擒別都盧、疏世利等四十二人，斬首三十五級，獲其二舟。

translations.literal: Fighting shifted to Shaozhou; the naturalized man Pan Dinggou climbed first, the troops advanced together, and Betudo, Shilishi, and forty-two others were captured alive; thirty-five heads were taken and two of their ships seized.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaozhou Pan Dinggou led the assault; forty-two including Betudo were captured, thirty-five heads taken, two ships seized.

sentences.zh: 餘賊復率三舟接戰。

translations.literal: The remaining rebels again led three ships to join battle.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors fought on with three ships.

sentences.zh: 應恩陣亡，賊亦敗遁。

translations.literal: Ying'en died in battle and the rebels also fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ying'en fell in battle and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 官軍得其礮，即名為佛郎機，副使汪鋐進之朝。

translations.literal: The government troops obtained their cannon and at once called them "Portuguese guns"; Vice Commissioner Wang Cheng presented them to court.
translations.idiomatic: The army captured their cannon, called them "Frankish guns," and Wang Cheng presented them to court.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，鋐累官右都御史，上言：「今塞上墩台城堡未嘗不設，乃冠來輒遭蹂躪者，蓋墩台止望，城堡又無制遠之具，故往往受困。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year Cheng, having risen to Right Censor-in-Chief, memorialized: "Today on the frontier the beacon towers and castles are not left unbuilt, yet whenever the enemy comes they are trampled—because towers only look out and castles lack means to strike far, so they are often trapped.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 9 Wang Cheng, now Right Censor-in-Chief, said frontier towers could not strike far and were often overrun.

sentences.zh: 當用臣所進郎機，其小止二十斤以下，遠可六百步者，則用之墩台。

translations.literal: The Portuguese guns I presented should be used: the small ones of no more than twenty catties, effective to six hundred paces, should be used on beacon towers.
translations.idiomatic: Use the Frankish guns I presented—those under twenty catties reaching six hundred paces—on the beacon towers.

sentences.zh: 每墩用其一，以三人守之。

translations.literal: Each tower should use one, guarded by three men.
translations.idiomatic: Each tower gets one gun manned by three men.

sentences.zh: 其大至七十斤以上，遠可五六里者，則用之城堡。

translations.literal: Those of seventy catties and above, effective to five or six li, should be used in castles.
translations.idiomatic: Guns of seventy catties reaching five or six li go to the castles.

sentences.zh: 每堡用其三，以十人守之。

translations.literal: Each castle should use three, guarded by ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Each castle gets three guns with ten guards.

sentences.zh: 五里一墩，十里一堡，大小相依，遠近相應，寇將無所容足，可坐收不戰之功。」

translations.literal: One tower every five li, one castle every ten li, large and small supporting each other, far and near responding—the enemy will have nowhere to set foot, and success may be won without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Towers every five li and castles every ten, mutually supporting, will leave the enemy nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，即從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and at once followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved at once.

sentences.zh: 火礮之有佛郎機自此始。

translations.literal: Cannon called "Portuguese guns" began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus began the "Frankish gun."

sentences.zh: 然將士不善用，迄莫能制寇也。

translations.literal: Yet officers and soldiers did not know how to use them well, and in the end could not control the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet troops never mastered them and could not defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 初，廣東文武官月俸多以番貨代，至是貨至者寡，有議復許佛郎機通市者。

translations.literal: At first Guangdong civil and military officials' monthly salaries were often paid in barbarian goods; by this time few goods arrived, and some proposed again allowing Portuguese trade.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong salaries had been paid in foreign goods; now some urged reopening Portuguese trade.

sentences.zh: 給事中王希文力爭，乃定令，諸番貢不以時及勘合差失者，悉行禁止，由是番舶幾絕。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Xiwen strove against it, and a regulation was fixed: all barbarian tribute not on schedule or with faulty tallies was wholly forbidden, and barbarian ships were nearly cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiwen blocked it; irregular tribute was banned and foreign shipping nearly ceased.

sentences.zh: 巡撫林富上言：「粵中公私諸費多資商稅，番舶不至，則公私皆窘。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lin Fu memorialized: "In Guangdong many public and private expenses depend on merchant taxes; if barbarian ships do not come, public and private affairs are both straitened.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fu said Guangdong's finances depended on maritime trade.

sentences.zh: 今許佛郎機互市有四利。

translations.literal: Now permitting Portuguese mutual trade has four benefits.
translations.idiomatic: Allowing Portuguese trade brings four benefits.

sentences.zh: 祖宗時諸番常貢外，原有抽分之法，稍取其餘，足供御用，利一。

translations.literal: Besides the regular tribute of the ancestors' time, there was originally a method of shares; taking a little of the remainder sufficed for imperial use—benefit one.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial shares from trade would supply the court—first benefit.

sentences.zh: 兩粵比歲用兵，庫藏耗竭，籍以充軍餉，備不虞，利二。

translations.literal: The two Guang provinces have used troops year after year and the treasury is drained; this can fill military pay and guard against emergencies—benefit two.
translations.idiomatic: It could fund the armies of both Guang provinces—second benefit.

sentences.zh: 粵西素仰給粵東，小有徵發，即措辦不前，若番舶流通，則上下交濟，利三。

translations.literal: Western Guang has long relied on Eastern Guang; at slight levies funds cannot be raised; if barbarian ships circulate, above and below will aid each other—benefit three.
translations.idiomatic: Western Guang could share Eastern Guang's prosperity—third benefit.

sentences.zh: 小民以懋遷為生，持一錢之貨，即得展轉販易，衣食其中，利四。

translations.literal: Common people live by trade; with one cash of goods they can turn merchandise and find food and clothing within it—benefit four.
translations.idiomatic: Small traders would thrive—fourth benefit.

sentences.zh: 助國裕民，兩有所賴，此因民之利而利之，非開利孔為民梯禍也。」

translations.literal: Aiding the state and enriching the people, both rely on this—this profits by the people's profit, not opening a profit gate to ladder calamity upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: This helps state and people alike without opening a door to disaster.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是佛郎機得入香山澳為市，而其徒又越境商於福建，往來不絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter Portugal could enter Xiangshan Ao to trade, and its people also crossed borders to trade in Fujian, coming and going without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Portugal then traded at Xiangshan Ao and Fujian without cease.

sentences.zh: 至二十六年，硃紈為巡撫，嚴禁通番。

translations.literal: By the twenty-sixth year Zhu Wan was grand coordinator and strictly forbade contact with barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 Grand Coordinator Zhu Wan banned foreign trade.

sentences.zh: 其人無所獲利，則整眾犯漳州之月港、浯嶼。

translations.literal: When they gained no profit, they gathered their host and attacked Yuegang and Wuyu in Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Denied profit, they raided Zhangzhou's Yuegang and Wuyu.

sentences.zh: 副使柯喬等御卻之。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Ke Qiao and others repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Qiao drove them off.

sentences.zh: 二十八年又犯詔安。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year they again attacked Zhao'an.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 they attacked Zhao'an.

sentences.zh: 官軍迎擊於走馬溪，生擒賊首李光頭等九十六人，余遁去。

translations.literal: Government troops met them at Zouma Creek and captured alive the bandit chief Li Guangtou and ninety-six others; the rest fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Zouma Creek troops captured Li Guangtou and ninety-six others.

sentences.zh: 紈用便宜斬之，怨紈者御史陳九德遂劾其專擅。

translations.literal: Wan executed them on his own authority; Censor Chen Jiude, who bore a grudge against Wan, then impeached him for arrogating power.
translations.idiomatic: Wan executed them summarily; Censor Chen Jiude impeached him for overreach.

sentences.zh: 帝遣給事中杜汝禎往驗，言此滿剌加商人，歲招海濱無賴之徒，往來鬻販，無僭號流劫事，紈擅自行誅，誠如御史所劾。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Supervising Secretary Du Ruzhen to investigate; he reported these were Malacca merchants who yearly recruited coastal ruffians to trade back and forth, with no usurped titles or plundering raids; Wan had indeed executed them on his own authority, just as the censor charged.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruzhen found them Malacca merchants, not pirates; Wan's executions were unlawful.

sentences.zh: 紈遂被逮，自殺。

translations.literal: Wan was then arrested and committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was arrested and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 蓋不知滿剌加即佛郎機也。

translations.literal: They did not know that Malacca was Portugal.
translations.idiomatic: They did not know Malacca meant Portugal.

sentences.zh: 自紈死。

translations.literal: After Wan's death,
translations.idiomatic: After Wan died,

sentences.zh: 海禁復弛，佛郎機遂縱橫海上無所忌。

translations.literal: the sea ban was again relaxed, and Portugal ranged the sea without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: the sea ban slackened and Portugal ranged the seas unchecked.

sentences.zh: 而其市香山澳、壕鏡者，至築室建城，雄踞海畔，若一國然，將吏不肖者反視為外府矣。

translations.literal: Those trading at Xiangshan Ao and Haojing even built houses and cities and sat powerfully on the shore like a separate state; unworthy officials treated them as an outer prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangshan and Macao they built cities like a foreign state; corrupt officials treated them as an outer prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壕鏡在香山縣南虎跳門外。

translations.literal: Haojing lies outside Hutiao Gate south of Xiangshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Macao lies south of Xiangshan beyond Hutiao Gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，暹羅、佔城、爪哇、琉球、浡泥諸國互市，俱在廣州，設市舶司領之。

translations.literal: Earlier Siam, Champa, Java, Ryukyu, Brunei, and other states traded at Guangzhou under the Maritime Trade Office.
translations.idiomatic: Siam, Champa, Java, Ryukyu, and Brunei had traded at Guangzhou under the Maritime Trade Office.

sentences.zh: 正德時，移於高州之電白縣。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period trade moved to Dianbai County in Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde trade moved to Dianbai in Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年，指揮黃慶納賄，請於上官，移之壕鏡，歲輸課二萬金，佛郎機遂得混入。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing Commander Huang Qing gave bribes and requested of superiors that trade be moved to Haojing with twenty thousand taels of gold yearly in tax; Portugal could then mix in.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 14 Huang Qing bribed superiors to move trade to Macao for twenty thousand gold in tax, letting Portugal in.

sentences.zh: 高棟飛甍，櫛比相望，閩、粵商人趨之若鶩。

translations.literal: Lofty beams and soaring eaves stood row on row; Fujian and Guangdong merchants hurried like ducks.
translations.idiomatic: Tall buildings rose thickly; Fujian and Guangdong merchants flocked there.

sentences.zh: 久之，其來益眾。

translations.literal: After long years their numbers grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: In time their numbers grew.

sentences.zh: 諸國人畏而避之，遂專為所據。

translations.literal: People of other states feared and avoided them, and they came to monopolize the place exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Other nations feared them and they monopolized the trade.

sentences.zh: 四十四年偽稱滿刺加入貢。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year they falsely claimed to be Malacca presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 they falsely claimed Malacca tribute.

sentences.zh: 已，改稱蒲都麗家。

translations.literal: Later they changed the name to Pudulijia.
translations.idiomatic: Later they called themselves Pudulijia.

sentences.zh: 守臣以聞，下部議，言必佛郎機假托，乃卻之。

translations.literal: Guarding officials reported it; the ministry deliberated and said it must be Portugal using a false name, and they were turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported it; the ministry recognized a Portuguese ruse and refused them.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，破滅呂宋，盡擅閩、粵海上之利，勢益熾。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period they destroyed Luzon and monopolized maritime profit in Fujian and Guangdong; their power grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli they destroyed Luzon and dominated Fujian and Guangdong trade.

sentences.zh: 至三十四年，又於隔水青州建寺，高六七丈，閎敞奇閟，非中國所有。

translations.literal: By the thirty-fourth year they also built a temple on Qingzhou across the water, six or seven zhang high, vast and strange, unlike anything in China.
translations.idiomatic: In year 34 they built a temple on Qingzhou, six or seven zhang high, unlike any Chinese building.

sentences.zh: 知縣張大猷請毀其高墉，不果。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhang Dayou asked to destroy their high walls, but it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhang Dayou asked to tear down their walls in vain.

sentences.zh: 明年，番禺舉人盧廷龍會試入都，請盡逐澳中諸番，出居浪白外海，還我壕鏡故地，當事不能用。

translations.literal: The next year Panyu licentiate Lu Tinglong, entering the capital for the metropolitan examination, asked that all barbarians in the settlement be driven out to trade beyond Langbai on the outer sea and Macao's old ground restored—the authorities could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Lu Tinglong petitioned to expel all foreigners from Macao; the court would not act.

sentences.zh: 番人既築城，聚海外雜番，廣通貿易，至萬餘人。

translations.literal: After the barbarians built their city they gathered overseas mixed barbarians and widely opened trade, reaching more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: They built a city, gathered ten thousand foreigners, and opened wide trade.

sentences.zh: 吏其土者，皆畏懼莫敢詰，甚有利其寶貨，佯禁而陰許之者。

translations.literal: Officials governing the place were all afraid and dared not investigate; some even coveted their treasures and goods, pretending to forbid while secretly allowing.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials feared them or secretly profited from their trade.

sentences.zh: 總督戴燿在事十三年，養成其患。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Dai Yao held office thirteen years and nurtured the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Dai Yao, in office thirteen years, let the trouble grow.

sentences.zh: 番人又潛匿倭賊，敵殺官軍。

translations.literal: The barbarians also secretly harbored Japanese pirates and killed government troops in enemy action.
translations.idiomatic: They also harbored Japanese pirates and killed soldiers.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，總督張鳴岡檄番人驅倭出海，因上言：「粵之有澳夷，猶疽之在背也。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year Grand Coordinator Zhang Minggang ordered the barbarians to drive the Japanese out to sea and memorialized: "Barbarians in the settlement in Guangdong are like a boil on the back.
translations.idiomatic: In year 42 Zhang Minggang made them expel the Japanese and said Macao was like a boil on Guangdong's back.

sentences.zh: 澳之有倭賊，猶虎之傅翼也。

translations.literal: Japanese pirates in the settlement are like a tiger given wings.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese there were a tiger given wings.

sentences.zh: 今一旦驅斥，不費一矢，此聖天子威德所致。

translations.literal: Now once driven off without costing a single arrow, this is due to the sage Son of Heaven's might and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Expelling them without a battle shows the emperor's power.

sentences.zh: 惟是倭去而番尚存，有謂宜剿除者，有謂宜移之浪白外洋就船貿易者，顧兵難輕動。

translations.literal: Only the Japanese are gone while the barbarians remain; some say they should be exterminated, some say moved to Langbai outer sea to trade from ships—but troops are hard to move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged extermination, others removal to outer Langbai—but war was risky.

sentences.zh: 而壕鏡在香山內地，官軍環海而守，彼日食所需，咸仰於我，一懷異志，我即制其死命。

translations.literal: Haojing lies within Xiangshan's inner lands; government troops ring the sea in guard; their daily food and needs all depend on us—if they harbor other intent, we at once control their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Macao lies inland; we supply their food and can destroy them at will.

sentences.zh: 若移之外洋，則巨海茫茫，奸宄安詰？

translations.literal: If moved to the outer sea, the great ocean is vast—how can treachery be examined?
translations.idiomatic: On the open sea, how could we control them?

sentences.zh: 制御安施？

translations.literal: How can control be applied?
translations.idiomatic: How enforce restraint?

sentences.zh: 似不如申明約束，內不許一奸闌出，外不許一倭闌入，無啟釁，無弛防，相安無患之為愈也。」

translations.literal: It seems better to declare constraints clearly: within, not one villain may slip out; without, not one Japanese may slip in; no provocation, no slack defense—peace without trouble is better.
translations.idiomatic: Better to bind them: no Chinese out, no Japanese in, strict defense, no trouble.

sentences.zh: 部議從之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry agreed.

sentences.zh: 居三年，設參將於中路雍陌營，調千人戍之，防禦漸密。

translations.literal: Three years later a deputy general was set at Zhonglu Yongmo camp with a thousand men garrisoned; defenses grew gradually tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later a garrison of a thousand tightened defenses.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，守臣慮其終為患，遣監司馮從龍等毀其所築青州城，番亦不敢拒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi guarding officials feared they would ultimately become a calamity and sent Supervisor Feng Conglong and others to destroy the Qingzhou city they had built; the barbarians also dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year 1 officials destroyed their Qingzhou city; the foreigners did not resist.

sentences.zh: 其時，大西洋人來中國，亦居此澳。

translations.literal: At that time people from the Great Western Ocean also came to China and lived in this settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Westerners from the Atlantic also settled there.

sentences.zh: 蓋番人本求市易，初無不軌謀，中朝疑之過甚，迄不許其朝貢，又無力以制之，故議者紛然。

translations.literal: The barbarians originally sought trade and at first had no rebellious designs; the central court suspected them excessively, never permitted their tribute, and also lacked strength to control them—hence disputants were many.
translations.idiomatic: They sought trade, not rebellion; excessive suspicion and weak control fueled endless debate.

sentences.zh: 然終明之世，此番固未嘗為變也。

translations.literal: Yet throughout the Ming dynasty these barbarians never in fact rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the whole Ming they never rebelled.

sentences.zh: 其人長身高鼻，貓晴鷹嘴，拳發赤須，好經商，恃強陵轢諸國，無所不往。

translations.literal: Their people are tall with high noses, cat's eyes and hawk beaks, curly red beards; they love trade and rely on strength to bully other states, going everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: They are tall, red-bearded traders who bullied every maritime state.

sentences.zh: 後又稱干係臘國。

translations.literal: Later they were also called the state of Ganxila.
translations.idiomatic: Later they were called Ganxila.

sentences.zh: 所產多犀象珠貝。

translations.literal: Their products are mostly rhinoceros, elephants, pearls, and shells.
translations.idiomatic: They traded rhinoceros horn, ivory, pearls, and shells.

sentences.zh: 衣服華潔，貴者冠，賤者笠，見尊長輒去之。

translations.literal: Clothing is splendid; the noble wear caps, the lowly bamboo hats, and before elders they remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Dress is fine; nobles wear caps, commoners hats, removed before elders.

sentences.zh: 初奉佛教，後奉天主教。

translations.literal: At first they followed Buddhism, later Catholicism.
translations.idiomatic: They were Buddhist, then Catholic.

sentences.zh: 市易但伸指示數，雖累千金不立約契，有事指天為誓，不相負。

translations.literal: In trade they only stretch out fingers to show numbers; though worth a thousand gold they make no written contract; for affairs they point to heaven in oath and do not betray each other.
translations.idiomatic: They counted on fingers, swore by heaven, and kept faith without written contracts.

sentences.zh: 自滅滿剌加、巴西、呂宋三國，海外諸蕃無敢與抗者。

translations.literal: Since destroying Malacca, Brazil, and Luzon, no overseas barbarian state dared resist them.
translations.idiomatic: After destroying Malacca, Brazil, and Luzon, none resisted them.

sentences.zh: 和蘭，又名紅毛番，地近佛郎機。

translations.literal: Holland, also called the Red-Haired Barbarians, lies near Portugal.
translations.idiomatic: Holland, the Red-Haired Barbarians, lies near Portugal.

sentences.zh: 永樂、宣德時，鄭和七下西洋，歷諸番數十國，無所謂和蘭者。

translations.literal: In the Yongle and Xuande periods Zheng He seven times went to the Western Ocean and passed dozens of barbarian states—there was no state called Holland.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng He's voyages listed no Holland.

sentences.zh: 其人深目長鼻，發眉須皆赤，足長尺二寸，頎偉倍常。

translations.literal: Their people have deep-set eyes and long noses; hair, brows, and beards are all red; feet are one foot two inches long; they are lofty, twice the usual size.
translations.idiomatic: They have deep eyes, red hair and beards, and unusually tall frames.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，福建商人歲給引往販大泥、呂宋及咬留吧者，和蘭人就諸國轉販，未敢窺中國也。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period Fujian merchants yearly received licenses to trade in Dani, Luzon, and Malacca; Hollanders went to those states to resell and did not yet dare peer at China.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli Fujian merchants traded in Southeast Asia; Dutch resold there but did not yet approach China.

sentences.zh: 自佛郎機市香山，據呂宋，和蘭聞而慕之。

translations.literal: When Portugal traded at Xiangshan and held Luzon, Holland heard and admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Portugal's hold on Xiangshan and Luzon drew Dutch envy.

sentences.zh: 二十九年駕大艦，攜巨礮，直薄呂宋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year they sailed great ships with huge cannon straight against Luzon.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 they sailed great ships with cannon against Luzon.

sentences.zh: 呂宋人力拒之，則轉薄香山澳。

translations.literal: The people of Luzon resisted strongly, so they turned against Xiangshan Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Luzon resisted; they turned to Xiangshan Ao.

sentences.zh: 澳中人數詰問，言欲通貢市，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: The people of the settlement questioned them in numbers; they said they wished to open tribute trade and dared not act as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Macao questioned them; they claimed to seek trade, not raid.

sentences.zh: 當事難之。

translations.literal: The authorities found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities hesitated.

sentences.zh: 稅使李道即召其酋入城，游處一月，不敢聞於朝，乃遣還。

translations.literal: Tax Commissioner Li Dao at once summoned their chief into the city, entertained him a month, dared not report to court, and then sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Tax Commissioner Li Dao entertained their chief a month in secret, then sent him away.

sentences.zh: 澳中人慮其登陸，謹防禦，始引去。

translations.literal: The people of the settlement, fearing they would land, guarded carefully and only then led them to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Macao guarded against landing until they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 海澄人李錦及奸商潘秀、郭震，久居大泥，與和蘭人習。

translations.literal: Haicheng man Li Jin and rogue merchants Pan Xiu and Guo Zhen had long lived in Dani and were familiar with Hollanders.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin, Pan Xiu, and Guo Zhen had long lived in Dani and knew the Dutch.

sentences.zh: 語及中國事，錦曰：「若欲通貢市，無若漳州者。

translations.literal: Speaking of China, Jin said: "If you wish to open tribute trade, none is like Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said: "For tribute trade, Zhangzhou is best.

sentences.zh: 漳南有彭湖嶼，去海遠，誠奪而守之，貢市不難成也。」

translations.literal: South of Zhangzhou is Penghu Island, far from the sea; truly seize and hold it and tribute trade is not hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Seize Penghu south of Zhangzhou and trade will follow.

sentences.zh: 其酋麻韋郎曰：「守臣不許，奈何？」

translations.literal: Their chief Ma Weilang said: "If guarding officials do not permit it, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ma Weilang asked what if officials refused.

sentences.zh: 曰：「稅使高采嗜金銀甚，若厚賄之，彼特疏上聞，天子必報可，守臣敢抗旨哉。」

translations.literal: He said: "Tax Commissioner Gao Cai loves gold and silver exceedingly; if you bribe him heavily, he will memorialize upward and the Son of Heaven will surely approve—how can guarding officials resist an imperial command?"
translations.idiomatic: Jin said bribing Tax Commissioner Gao Cai would secure imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 酋曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The chief said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The chief agreed.

sentences.zh: 錦乃代為大泥國王書，一移采，一移兵備副使，一移守將，俾秀、震齎以來。

translations.literal: Jin then wrote letters in the name of the king of Dani—one to Cai, one to the vice commissioner of military supplies, one to the guarding general—and had Xiu and Zhen carry them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forged letters as Dani's king to Cai, the vice commissioner, and the general.
