sentences.zh: 守將陶拱聖大駭，亟白當事，系秀於獄，震遂不敢入。

translations.literal: Guarding General Tao Gongxian was greatly alarmed, quickly informed the authorities, and imprisoned Xiu; Zhen then dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: General Tao Gongxian imprisoned Pan Xiu; Guo Zhen did not come.

sentences.zh: 初，秀與酋約，入閩有成議，當遣舟相聞，而酋卞急不能待，即駕二大艦，直抵彭湖。

translations.literal: At first Xiu had agreed with the chief that when entry to Fujian succeeded they would send a boat to announce it, but the chief was impatient and could not wait; he at once sailed two great ships straight to Penghu.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xiu had promised notice on success, but the Dutch sailed straight to Penghu.

sentences.zh: 時三十二年之七月。

translations.literal: It was the seventh month of the thirty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: It was the seventh month of year 32.

sentences.zh: 汛兵已撤，如入無人之墟，遂伐木築舍為久居計。

translations.literal: Seasonal troops had withdrawn; it was like entering an empty place, and they felled timber and built shelters planning long residence.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons were withdrawn; they built on Penghu as if unoccupied.

sentences.zh: 錦亦潛入漳州偵探，詭言被獲逃還，當事已廉知其狀，並系獄。

translations.literal: Jin also secretly entered Zhangzhou to spy, falsely saying he had been captured and escaped; the authorities already knew his situation and imprisoned him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jin spied in Zhangzhou and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 已而議遣二人諭其酋還國，許以自贖，且拘震與俱。

translations.literal: Then it was proposed to send two men to instruct the chief to return home, permitting ransom, and also to detain Zhen with them.
translations.idiomatic: Two men were sent to order the Dutch home and detain Guo Zhen.

sentences.zh: 三人既與酋成約，不欲自彰其失，第雲「我國尚依違未定」。

translations.literal: The three had made terms with the chief and did not wish to expose their fault; they only said "Our country is still undecided."
translations.idiomatic: The envoys, bound to the Dutch, only said their country was undecided.

sentences.zh: 而當事所遣將校詹獻忠齎檄往諭者，乃多攜幣帛、食物，覬其厚酬。

translations.literal: Yet the military officers the authorities sent, Zhan Xianzhong carrying proclamations to instruct them, mostly carried silks, food, and goods, hoping for heavy reward.
translations.idiomatic: Officer Zhan Xianzhong brought gifts hoping for Dutch payment.

sentences.zh: 海濱人又潛載貨物往市，酋益觀望不肯去。

translations.literal: Coastal people also secretly carried goods to trade; the chief grew more watchful and would not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal traders dealt with them; the Dutch refused to go.

sentences.zh: 當事屢遣使諭之，見酋語輒不競，愈為所慢。

translations.literal: The authorities repeatedly sent envoys to instruct them; whenever they met the chief they did not contend in speech and were increasingly despised by him.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated missions were humiliated by the Dutch chief.

sentences.zh: 而采己遣心腹周之范詣酋，說以三萬金饋采，即許貢市，酋喜與之。

translations.literal: Cai had already sent his confidant Zhou Zhifan to the chief, saying thirty thousand gold presented to Cai would secure tribute trade; the chief gladly agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cai's agent Zhou Zhifan promised trade for thirty thousand gold; the chief agreed.

sentences.zh: 盟已就矣，會總兵施德政令都司沈有容將兵往諭。

translations.literal: The alliance was already made when Regional Commander Shi Dezheng ordered Division Commander Shen Yourong to lead troops to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: When the pact was made, Shen Yourong was sent with troops.

sentences.zh: 有容負膽智，大聲論說，酋心折，乃曰：「我從不聞此言。」

translations.literal: Yourong had daring and wisdom; speaking loudly in argument, the chief's heart was won over, and he said: "I have never heard such words."
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yourong spoke boldly; the chief was impressed and said he had never heard such words.

sentences.zh: 其下人露刃相詰，有容無所懾，盛氣與辨，酋乃悔悟，令之范還所贈金，止以哆囉嗹、玻璃器及番刀、番酒饋采，乞代奏通市。

translations.literal: His subordinates bared blades and pressed him; Yourong was not intimidated, spoke with full spirit in debate, and the chief then repented, ordered Zhifan to return the gold given, and only presented to Cai porcelain, glassware, barbarian swords, and barbarian wine, begging him to memorialize for opening trade.
translations.idiomatic: His men drew blades; Yourong stood firm, and the chief repented, took back Zhou's gold, gave Cai lesser gifts, and begged trade be reported.

sentences.zh: 采不敢應，而撫、按嚴禁奸民下海，犯者必誅，由是接濟路窮，番人無所得食，十月末揚帆去。

translations.literal: Cai dared not agree, while the grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner strictly forbade traitors going to sea—violators were surely executed—so the supply route was cut off, the barbarians had no food, and at the end of the tenth month they raised sails and left.
translations.idiomatic: Cai dared not agree; coastal trade was banned; the Dutch starved and sailed away in late tenth month.

sentences.zh: 巡撫徐學聚劾秀、錦等罪，論死、遣戍有差。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xu Xueju impeached Xiu, Jin, and others; death sentences and banishment were assigned in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xueju condemned Pan Xiu, Li Jin, and others to death or exile.

sentences.zh: 然是時佛郎機橫海上，紅毛與爭雄，復泛舟東來，攻破美洛居國，與佛郎機分地而守。

translations.literal: Yet at that time Portugal ranged the sea; the Red-Hairs contended for mastery and again sailed east, smashed the state of Meilüju, and divided territory with Portugal to guard.
translations.idiomatic: Portugal ruled the seas; the Dutch fought them, seized Meilüju, and shared territory.

sentences.zh: 後又侵奪台灣地，築室耕田，久留不去，海上奸民，闌出貨物與市。

translations.literal: Later they again seized Taiwan, built houses and cultivated fields, and long remained without leaving; coastal traitors slipped out goods to trade with them.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Taiwan, farmed there, and Chinese smugglers traded with them.

sentences.zh: 已，又出據彭湖，築城設守，漸為求市計。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they again came out and held Penghu, built a city and set guards, and gradually planned to seek trade.
translations.idiomatic: They reoccupied Penghu, fortified it, and sought trade.

sentences.zh: 守臣懼禍，說以毀城遠徙，即許互市。

translations.literal: Guarding officials feared calamity and persuaded them that if they destroyed the city and moved far away, trade would be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, fearing war, promised trade if they abandoned Penghu.

sentences.zh: 番人從之，天啟三年果毀其城，移舟去。

translations.literal: The barbarians followed this; in the third year of Tianqi they indeed destroyed their city and moved their ships away.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed; in Tianqi year 3 they destroyed Penghu and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 巡撫商周祚以遵諭遠徙上聞，然其據台灣自若也。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Shang Zhouzuo reported obedience to instruction and distant removal upward, yet they held Taiwan as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Zhouzuo reported their withdrawal, but they still held Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 已而互市不成，番人怨，復築城彭湖，掠漁舟六百餘艘，俾華人運土石助築。

translations.literal: When mutual trade was not achieved the barbarians were resentful; they again built a city at Penghu, seized more than six hundred fishing boats, and made Chinese transport earth and stone to help build.
translations.idiomatic: Trade failed; they rebuilt Penghu, seized six hundred fishing boats, and forced Chinese to build.

sentences.zh: 尋犯廈門，官軍御之，俘斬數十人，乃詭詞求款。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they invaded Xiamen; government troops resisted them, captured and beheaded several tens, and they then used false words to seek a truce.
translations.idiomatic: They raided Xiamen, lost dozens killed, then sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 再許毀城遠徙，而修築如故。

translations.literal: Again they promised to destroy the city and move far away, yet repaired and built as before.
translations.idiomatic: They promised to leave Penghu but kept building.

sentences.zh: 已，又泊風櫃仔，出沒浯嶼、白坑、東椗、莆頭、古雷、洪嶼、沙洲、甲洲間，要求互市。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they anchored at Fengguizi, appearing and disappearing among Wuyu, Baikeng, Dongding, Putou, Gulei, Hongyu, Shazhou, Jiazhou, demanding mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: They anchored at Fengguizi and ranged the coast demanding trade.

sentences.zh: 而海寇李旦復助之，濱海郡邑為戒嚴。

translations.literal: Sea bandit Li Dan again aided them, and coastal prefectures and counties were put on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Pirate Li Dan aided them; coastal districts went on alert.

sentences.zh: 其年，巡撫南居益初至，謀討之。

translations.literal: That year Grand Coordinator Nan Juyi had just arrived and planned to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: That year Nan Juyi arrived and planned an attack.

sentences.zh: 上言：「臣入境以來，聞番船五艘續至，與風櫃仔船合，凡十有一艘，其勢愈熾。

translations.literal: He memorialized upward: "Since I entered my jurisdiction I have heard that five barbarian ships have continued to arrive and joined the Fengguizi ships—eleven in all—and their power grows still fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: He reported eleven Dutch ships had gathered and their strength grew.

sentences.zh: 有小校陳士瑛者，先遣往咬留吧宣諭其王，至三角嶼遇紅毛船，言咬留吧王已往阿南國，因與士瑛偕至大泥，謁其王。

translations.literal: Junior officer Chen Shiying had first been sent to Malacca to instruct its king; at Sanjiaozhou he met a Red-Hair ship, which said the king of Malacca had gone to Anan, and therefore went with Shiying to Dani and had audience with its king.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shiying met Dutch ships en route to Malacca and went on to Dani.

sentences.zh: 王言咬留吧國主已大集戰艦，議往彭湖求互市，若不見許，必至構兵。

translations.literal: The king said the lord of Malacca had already gathered warships in great array and planned to go to Penghu to seek mutual trade; if not permitted, he would surely raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Dani's king said Malacca would attack Penghu if trade were denied.

sentences.zh: 蓋阿南即紅毛番國，而咬留吧、大泥與之合謀，必不可以理諭。

translations.literal: Anan is the Red-Hair barbarian state, and Malacca and Dani join in plot with it—they cannot be instructed by reason.
translations.idiomatic: Anan is Holland; Malacca and Dani plot with it—reason will not avail.

sentences.zh: 為今日計，非用兵不可。」

translations.literal: For today's plan, war is unavoidable.
translations.idiomatic: War is unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 因列上調兵足餉方略，部議從之。

translations.literal: He therefore listed strategies for transferring troops and supplying provisions; the ministry deliberated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed troop and supply plans; the ministry approved.

sentences.zh: 四年正月遣將先奪鎮海港而城之，且築且戰，番人乃退守風櫃城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year troops were first sent to seize Zhenhai Harbor and build a city there; building and fighting together, the barbarians then retreated to defend Fengguizi city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, month 1, troops seized Zhenhai and built a fort; the Dutch retreated to Fengguizi.

sentences.zh: 居益增兵往助，攻擊數月，寇猶不退，乃大發兵，諸軍齊進。

translations.literal: Juyi added troops to assist; after attacking several months the raiders still did not retreat, and troops were greatly increased, all armies advancing together.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Juyi reinforced the attack for months, then launched a general assault.

sentences.zh: 寇勢窘，兩遣使求緩兵，容運米入舟即退去。

translations.literal: The raiders' situation was desperate; twice they sent envoys begging a truce, asking only to load rice into boats and then withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The Dutch, trapped, twice begged time to load rice and leave.

sentences.zh: 諸將以窮寇莫追，許之，遂揚帆去。

translations.literal: The generals said a cornered enemy should not be pursued and permitted it; they then raised sails and left.
translations.idiomatic: Generals let them sail away unmolested.

sentences.zh: 獨渠帥高文律等十二人據高樓自守，諸將破擒之，獻俘於朝。

translations.literal: Only the bandit chief Gao Wenlü and twelve others held a high tower and defended themselves; the generals broke in and captured them and presented the captives at court.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve leaders including Gao Wenlü held out and were captured for the capital.

sentences.zh: 彭湖之警以息，而其據台灣者猶自若也。

translations.literal: The Penghu alarm thus ceased, yet those holding Taiwan remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Penghu was quiet, but Taiwan remained Dutch.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，為鄭芝龍所破，不敢窺內地者數年，乃與香山佛郎機通好，私貿外洋。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period they were broken by Zheng Zhilong and for several years did not dare peer at the inner lands; they then made friends with the Portuguese of Xiangshan and privately traded on the outer ocean.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen Zheng Zhilong defeated them; they then traded secretly with Macao's Portuguese.

sentences.zh: 十年駕四舶，由虎跳門薄廣州，聲言求市。

translations.literal: In the tenth year four ships came by Hutiao Gate against Guangzhou, declaring they sought trade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 four ships came to Guangzhou seeking trade.

sentences.zh: 其酋招搖市上，奸民視之若金穴，蓋大姓有為之主者。

translations.literal: Their chief swaggered in the market; traitors looked on it as a gold mine—for great clans had patrons behind it.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief traded openly; great families profited as patrons.

sentences.zh: 當道鑑壕鏡事，議驅斥，或從中撓之。

translations.literal: Local authorities, seeing Macao's lesson, debated expulsion, but some interfered from within.
translations.idiomatic: Officials debated expulsion, but some blocked it.

sentences.zh: 會總督張鏡心初至，力持不可，乃遁去。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jingxin had just arrived and firmly held it impossible; they then slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zhang Jingxin refused trade and they left.

sentences.zh: 已，為奸民李葉榮所誘，交通總兵陳謙為居停出入。

translations.literal: Later they were enticed by traitor Li Yerong, who dealt through Regional Commander Chen Qian as host for coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Yerong used General Chen Qian as go-between.

sentences.zh: 事露，葉榮下吏。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Yerong was handed to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yerong was arrested.

sentences.zh: 謙自請調用以避禍，為兵科凌義渠等所劾，坐逮訊。

translations.literal: Qian himself requested transfer to avoid calamity and was impeached by the military section Ling Yiqu and others; he was arrested and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qian sought transfer, was impeached, and arrested.

sentences.zh: 自是，奸民知事終不成，不復敢勾引，而番人猶據台灣自若。

translations.literal: From then on traitors knew the affair could not succeed and no longer dared to entice them, yet the barbarians still held Taiwan as before.
translations.idiomatic: Smugglers ceased enticing them, but they still held Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 其本國在西洋者，去中華絕遠，華人未嘗至。

translations.literal: Their original country in the Western Ocean is extremely far from China; Chinese have never been there.
translations.idiomatic: Their homeland in Europe lies beyond Chinese reach.

sentences.zh: 其所恃惟巨舟大礮。

translations.literal: What they rely on is only great ships and large cannon.
translations.idiomatic: They depend on great ships and heavy guns.

sentences.zh: 舟長三十丈，廣六丈，厚二尺餘，樹五桅，後為三層樓。

translations.literal: Ships are thirty zhang long, six zhang wide, more than two chi thick; five masts are set, and behind is a three-storied tower.
translations.idiomatic: Their ships are thirty zhang long, six wide, with five masts and a three-deck stern.

sentences.zh: 旁設小囪置銅礮。

translations.literal: Small funnels are set at the sides with bronze cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze guns stand in side ports.

sentences.zh: 桅下置二丈巨鐵礮，發之可洞裂石城，震數十里，世所稱紅夷礮，即其制也。

translations.literal: Below the mast is placed a great iron cannon two zhang in size; fired, it can pierce stone walls and shake for several tens of li—the so-called Red-Barbarian cannon of the age is of this make.
translations.idiomatic: Two-zhang iron guns beneath the mast shatter stone walls—the famed Red-Barbarian cannon.

sentences.zh: 然以舟大難轉，或遇淺沙，即不能動。

translations.literal: Yet because the ships are large they are hard to turn, and if they meet shallow sand they cannot move at all.
translations.idiomatic: Great ships turn poorly and ground on shoals.

sentences.zh: 而其人又不善戰，故往往挫衄。

translations.literal: Their people are also not skilled at fighting, so they are often defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fight poorly and often lose.

sentences.zh: 其所役使名烏鬼。

translations.literal: Those they employ are called "black ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: They employ slaves called "black ghosts."

sentences.zh: 入水不沉，走海面若平地。

translations.literal: They do not sink in water and run on the sea surface like level ground.
translations.idiomatic: These divers do not sink and run on water like land.

sentences.zh: 其柁後置照海鏡，大徑數尺，能照數百里。

translations.literal: Behind the rudder is placed a sea-mirror, several chi in diameter, able to illuminate several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: A great "sea mirror" astern can sight hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 其人悉奉天主教。

translations.literal: Their people all follow Catholicism.
translations.idiomatic: They are all Catholic.

sentences.zh: 所產有金、銀、琥珀、瑪瑙、玻璃、天鵝絨、瑣服、哆囉嗹。

translations.literal: Products include gold, silver, amber, agate, glass, swansdown, filigree garments, and porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: They produce gold, silver, amber, agate, glass, down, filigree, and porcelain.

sentences.zh: 國土既富，遇中國貨物當意者，不惜厚資，故華人樂與為市。

translations.literal: The country is rich; when Chinese goods please them they do not spare heavy payment, so Chinese are glad to trade with them.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm is rich and pays well for Chinese goods, so Chinese gladly trade with them.
